title: Barkley ES Stairwells Replacement
description: Construction of the Barkley Elementary School Stairwells Replacement at Fort Campbell, KY. A market survey is being conducted to determine if there are a reasonable number of interested business concerns to determine any future set-asides for this project. If your firm is a Small Business, certified HUBZone, 8A, Woman-Owned Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, or Large Business and you are interested in this project please respond appropriately. The intent of this future solicitation will be to select one contractor for the design-bid-build construction of the Barkley Elementary School Stairwells Replacement at Fort Campbell, KY. Project Location: Fort Campbell, KY 37042 Project Description: Construction of four (4) 357 square foot exterior stairwells totaling 1,428 Square Feet at Barkley Elementary School at Ft. Campbell, KY. Barkley Elementary School has four exterior stairwells that have been damaged by snow removal salt. These stairwells are painted steel beams and steel pans (pans are concrete filled steps), that have rust damage. A recent project to sandblast and epoxy paint the steel portions of the stairwells was unsuccessful; severe rusting and degradation of the steel stairwells continued after the next salt placement for snow removal. Contract duration is estimated at 180 calendar days. In accordance with FAR 36.204, the estimated cost range is $500,000.00-$1,000,000. The NAICS code is 238190 - Other Foundation, Structure, and Building Exterior Contractors with a Size Standard of $19M. All interested Small Businesses, certified HUBZONE, 8A, Woman-Owned Small Businesses, and Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business contractors should respond to this survey via the Microsoft Forms link NLT 30 November 2026 by 11:00 AM Eastern Time. This project will be solicitated as a single-phase design-bid-build project. Responses should include: 1. Identification and verification of the company�s small business status. 2. Contractor�s Unique Identifier Number and CAGE Code(s). 3. Documentation from the firm�s bonding company showing current single and aggregate performance and payment bond limits. 4. Descriptions of Experience � Interested construction firms must provide no more than three (3) example projects with greater than 95 percent completion or projects completed in the past five (5) years in which the interested firm served as the prime contractor. Example projects must be of similar size and scope to be considered. Each project must include the name, title, project role, e-mail address, and telephone number of at least one reference that may be contacted to verify project size, scope, dollar value, self-performance percentage, percent complete, and quality of performance.. a. Projects considered similar in scope to this project would include Steel fabrication and erection above single-story height or similar exterior stairwell replacement or new installation. b. Projects considered similar in size to this project would include: Steel Fabrication over 800 sq. ft.. c. Based on the information above, for each project submitted, include: 1. Current percentage of construction complete and the date when it was or will be completed. 2. Scope of the project. 3. Size of the project. 5. The dollar value of the construction contract and whether it was design-bid build, design-build or design-build to budget. 6. The percentage of work that was self-performed as project and/or construction management services or physical construction type work. 7. Identify the number of subcontractors by construction trade utilized for each project. 8. Documentation from the firm�s bonding company showing current single and aggregate performance and payment bond limits. 9. Small Businesses are reminded under RFO 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting; they must perform at least 15% of the cost of the contract, not including the cost of materials, with the firm�s own employees for general construction-type procurement. Include the percentage of work that will be self-performed on this project, and how it will be accomplished. Submission Requirement: The only authorized transmission method of responses is via filling out the survey form. No other transmission method will be accepted. Please limit your capability statement to the space provided within the form. The Market Survey Form can be accessed at https://forms.osi.apps.mil/Pages/DesignPageV2.aspx?origin=ShareFormPage&subpage=design&m2=1&id=unZN_HzxUEy5p48xY9J1gs_kFZkiSvdBsl16R5WGbRZUM1Q5TFhIVElUWFJDNDBOMFdSNFBDTEVLSS4u or via the QR Code provided below: This is NOT a Request for Proposal and does not constitute any commitment by the Government. Responses to this sources sought notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. All interested sources must respond to future solicitation announcements separately for responses to this market survey. NOTICE: The following information is provided for situational awareness and is not required to respond to this Sources Sought. All contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (www.SAM.gov) prior to award of a contract. All proposed contractors are highly encouraged to review FAR Clause 52.232-33 Payments by Electronic Funds Transfer � System for Award Management, which indicates �All payments by the Government under this contract shall be made by electronic funds transfer (EFT).� Those not currently registered can obtain registration by going to the website http://www.SAM.gov. The process can usually be completed from 24 to 48 hours after submission. Contractors will need to obtain a Unique Entity Identifier (formerly DUNS number) for processing their registration. If you do not already have a Unique Entity Identifier, one can be obtained from http://www.SAM.gov. Refer to www.SAM.gov for information formerly found in CCR, EPLS, ORCA and FedReg. Please begin the registration process immediately to avoid delay of the contract award should your firm be selected. ALERT: You must submit a notarized letter appointing the authorized Entity Administrator before your registration will be activated. This requirement now applies to both new and existing entities. Effective 29 April 2018, the notarized letter process is now mandatory on all CURRENT registrants at SAM who have a requirement to update data on their SAM record. The notarized letter is mandatory and is required before the GSA Federal Service Desk (FSD) will activate the entity's registration. Effective 29 June 2018, vendors creating or updating their registration can have their registration activated prior to the approval of the required notarized letter. However, the signed copy of the notarized letter must be sent to the GSA Federal Service Desk (FSD) within 30 days of activation or the vendor risks no longer being active in SAM. Vendors can check whether an account is active by performing a query by their CAGE or Unique Entity Identifier The new registration process may now take several weeks, so vendors are highly encouraged to begin registering as soon as possible to avoid any possible delays in future contract awards. Remember, there is no cost to use SAM. To find out additional information about the changes of the SAM registration process, contractors should visit the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) link located at the top of the SAM homepage (www.sam.gov).

title: J041--Service - AHU PM & Filter Evaluation - NWI
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Omaha and Grand Island VAMC - HVAC Preventive Maintenance and Filter Evaluation NAICS: 238220 - PSC: J041 - Small Business Size Standard: $19 million NOTICE PURPOSE The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 23, is conducting market research to identify businesses capable of providing HVAC preventive maintenance and filter evaluation services at the Omaha and Grand Island VA Medical Centers. This is a sources sought notice only and is not a solicitation or request for quotations. No award will be made from responses, and the Government will not reimburse response costs. GENERAL REQUIREMENT The anticipated requirement includes: Preventive maintenance and inspections of air handling units (AHUs) and rooftop units (RTUs). HVAC equipment and coil cleaning. Air filter inspections and evaluations. Airflow and system performance testing. Humidifier inspection and maintenance. HEPA/MERV filter evaluation and applicable replacement work. Written reports documenting inspections, maintenance, and deficiencies. Services are anticipated for a base year with option years. The detailed requirements will be provided in any resulting solicitation. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE Omaha VA Medical Center, 4101 Woolworth Avenue, Omaha, NE 68105 Grand Island VA Medical Center, 2201 N Broadwell Avenue, Grand Island, NE 68803 INFORMATION REQUESTED Company name, address, UEI, and point of contact with phone number and email. Business size and socioeconomic status, including SBA-certified SDVOSB or VOSB status. Confirmation that the company can perform the services described above at both locations. Brief description of similar HVAC preventive maintenance experience. Whether services would be performed by company employees, subcontractors, or both. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Email responses no later than Monday, November 30, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. Central Time to amanda.patterson-elliott@va.gov. Use "Omaha and Grand Island HVAC PM Sources Sought" in the subject line. NO PHONE CALL, PLEASE. Responses are for market research purposes only and do not constitute offers.

description: Title: Reagent Generation for Bioanalytical Method Development on Biologics Therapeutics This is a Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential requirement. This notice is issued to help determine the availability of qualified companies technically capable of meeting the Government requirement and to determine the method of acquisition. It is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. The Government is especially interested in determining (1) the availability of qualified small business sources; (2) whether they are small businesses; HUBZone small businesses; service-disabled, veteran-owned small businesses; 8(a) small businesses; veteran-owned small businesses; woman-owned small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; and (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition (5) commercial product and services availability. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. Background: The Therapeutic Development Branch (TDB) within the Division of Preclinical Innovation (DPI) at National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS), National Institutes of Health (NIH) conducts translational research in the area of human therapeutics development by moving small molecule and biologic drug candidates forward in the drug development pipeline. Upon reaching predetermined milestones, TDB hands off clinical candidates to external partners to bring these novel therapies to patients. In addition to developing new candidate drugs, TDB seeks to advance the entire field of drug discovery and development by encouraging scientific and technological innovations aimed at improving success rates in the crucial preclinical stage of drug development. The TDB model is to operate as a comprehensive small molecule and biologics drug development organization, moving therapeutic candidates through each phase of the preclinical development process until an Investigational New Drug (IND) application is filed with the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA). TDB conducts drug development as collaborations, with therapeutic candidates originating from academia, industry, non- profit foundations, or internally from NCATS and other NIH Institutes and Centers. TDB�s operational strategy is to combine the capabilities of in-house staff and collaborative partners with complementary support from contract research organizations (CROs). Each development program operates in a multi-disciplinary matrix team environment, with NCATS responsible for the overall planning and execution. Please see the attachment for more details.

title: Progressive Design-Build (PDB) - USSF Integration Facility F/10852 at WPAFB
description: SPECIAL NOTICE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is issuing this special notice to announce an upcoming competition for a design and construction solicitation for the US Space Force Integration Facility, F/10852 using Progressive Design-Build under 10 USC �2808a Other Transaction Authority for Construction. This notice is for informational and planning purposes to allow interested parties to prepare for and provide feedback prior to the official solicitation release. I. INDUSTRY DAY USACE intends to conduct an Industry Day on 03 December 2026 at 0900 Eastern Time to provide an overview of the project, acquisition strategy, and anticipated requirements. This event will provide interested parties with an opportunity to gain additional insight into the project and proposed PDB under an OT (non-FAR-based) framework. A notional acquisition schedule will be shared. Interested parties are encouraged to ask questions and provide input. General questions will be permitted during the Industry Day; however, all discussions and responses provided during the event are considered unofficial and are for informational purposes only. Statements made during the Industry Day do not constitute commitment, authorization, or binding guidance related to the future RFQ. Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) will be accepted and addressed following the release of RFQ. II. LOCATION Industry Day Presentation location: Hope Hotel, 10823 Chidlaw Rd # A, Dayton, OH 45433 III. PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: US Space Force Integration Facility, F/10852 Location: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), OH NAICS Code: 236220 Total Program Funding: $394,000,000.00 IV. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The USSF Integration Facility is a newly programmed mission at Wright-Patterson Air Force WPAFB, Ohio. It serves as a highly classified and secured contiguous operations area to enable Director for National Intelligence (DNI) and United States Space Force (USSF) directed and endorsed missions in areas of the highest national security, housing intelligence analysis and production for new and expanded all-source means that enable near-real-time capabilities. The facility supports the intelligence needs of the Defense Intelligence Enterprise, USSF, joint warfighters, policymakers, and acquisition professionals, driving intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) for space domain operations including detection, characterization, and targeting of adversary space capabilities. The adjacent existing facility, Building F/10854, will remain fully occupied and uninterrupted, maintaining 24/7 business operations and ICD 705 security accreditation throughout construction, requiring strict utility, access, physical security, and logistical phasing constraints. Construction is broken into distinct agreement phases under the Progressive Design-Build (PDB) framework. Phase 1 (Design & Pre-Construction): This Phase is structured to collaboratively advance the facility design from initial concepts to 65% design maturity, perform detailed constructability reviews, conduct transparent open-book cost estimating, identify and mitigate complex interface risks, and validate the overall space programming. Pre-construction services will establish a baseline cost and allow for early design and potential separate authorization of long-lead procurement items. Phase 2 (Final Design and Construction): This Phase will include the completion of final design documents (95% and 100% Certified Final), fast-tracking capabilities, and all physical construction activities, including structural, interior finishes, specialized secure Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) fit-out, redundant systems commissioning, and final security accreditation. Phase 2 will also include comprehensive site work, utility distribution integration, and connection into the active Building F/10854. Phase 2 covers construction of the multi-floor, approximately 333,700 SF secure USSF Integration Facility, including the physical connection to active Building F/10854, the integration of high-efficiency HVAC networks, a backup generator facility, high-security electrical switchgear, and the buildout of specialized SCIF and SAP compartments. The Government will use available concept design information, programmed requirements, and initial planning data as the initial technical baseline. During Phase 1, the selected Design-Builder will validate the baseline and may recommend refinements; any material deviation from the Government�s baseline will require Government review and approval. The scope generally encompasses the following critical lines of effort: Critical Infrastructure and Utilities: Installation of high-efficiency mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems designed for 24/7 continuous operation, electrical tie-ins to centralized utilities, backup generator integration (7,500 KW), Lightning Protection Systems (LPS), and addressable fire protection networks. Secure Facilities: Turnkey design, construction, and Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) accreditation of highly classified Special Access Program (SAP) SCIF spaces built to stringent ICD 705, IC Tech Spec, and Telecommunictaions Electronics Material Protected from Emanating Spurious Tranmission (TEMPEST) shielding standards to ensure complete physical, visual, and acoustic isolation. New Construction, Envelope, and Physical Connection: Construction of a new structural frame with metal panels and pre-cast exterior walls, establishing a secure thermal wall envelope, executing the physical and utility connection to adjacent operational Building F/10854, and conducting all associated site work, paving, and access control infrastructure. V. ACQUISITION STRATEGY - PRE-AWARD The USACE will use a streamlined competitive selection process: Step 1 �RFQ: Interested parties will submit a Statement of Qualifications (SOQ). Following evaluation of the qualification packages, the Government intends to short-list a target of three (3) of the highest qualified Design-Builders to proceed to Step 2. Step 2 � Pitches: Selected Companies will participate in pitch presentations. One company will be selected as the Design-Build team for award of the initial design and preconstruction services with a modification for design completion and construction award. Step 3 � Exclusive Negotiation: Based on pitch evaluations, the Government will select one Design-Builder to enter exclusive negotiations. VI. ACQUSITION STRATEGY � AWARD The agreement will be awarded to the most qualified Progressive Design-Build Entity (PDBE) to provide design development, preconstruction services, and construction. Post-award Phase 1 of PDB includes Design and Pre-construction services and Post-award Phase 2 includes the final design and construction. The agreement will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). The FFP for successive design and construction milestones will be agreed to as the design progresses and funds are available. VII. VIRTUAL PARTICIPATION OPPORTUNITY: For those who are unable to attend the Industry Day event in person, the Louisville District will also make the event available via Microsoft Teams. The details related to the MS Teams event are provided below: Microsoft Teams Meeting Join: https://dod.teams.microsoft.us/meet/993610255621?p=yaQ28DL3lmCC9Nap5C Meeting ID: 993 610 255 621 Passcode: Y6sB764r VIII. KEY SECURITY REQUIREMENTS This project will require the selected contractor and its subcontractor(s) to process, store, or transmit CUI and Federal Contract Information (FCI). In accordance with the CMMC program (32 CFR part 170) and USACE policy (including Alert 26-HQ-010, Rev1), CMMC Level 2 (Self) will be a mandatory prerequisite prior to award. Offerors must have an active SAM registration and a current, verified BASIC confidence level assessment (or higher) posted in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) in accordance with NIST SP 800-171. description: Request for Information 36C10B27Q0010 Page 2 of 2 Request for Information 36C10B27Q0010 Enterprise Database Vulnerability Scanning Solution INTRODUCTION This is a Request for Information (RFI) notice for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation, or a Request for Proposal. Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products described in this notice. Your response to this RFI notice will be treated only as information for the Government to consider. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI notice. Specifically, the requirement for at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing or 50% of the services be performed by yourself and/or other eligible and Small Business Administration verified SDVOSB/VOSB concerns; and certification from the Small Business Administration (VetCert). It is requested that all companies interested in participating in this RFI please note their interest and provide indication of their respective capabilities to perform the potential effort, as described in the paragraphs below and the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) Description. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI notice is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. VA reserves the right to not respond to any, all, or select responses or materials submitted. All requirements identified herein are subject to change at any time. The purpose of this RFI notice is for planning purposes, to identify market information and qualified contractors who are able to meet VA s requirement for Enterprise Database Vulnerability Scanning Solution. Any information provided in response to this RFI notice may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy and Performance Work Statement, as well as determining any set-aside decisions. BACKGROUND: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information and Technology, Cybersecurity Operations Center (CSOC), requires an enterprise database vulnerability scanning solution to support recurring security assessments and Authorization to Operate (ATO) activities. VA currently uses LevelBlue Trustwave DbProtect across four production environments and one development environment. The existing capability includes centralized management, distributed scanning, vulnerability assessment content, reporting and analytics, and supporting repository and data-processing functions. Scanning components operate on premises and within VA Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft Azure environments. Management, reporting, and repository functions are hosted on premises. The current repository retains 12 months of scan information and uses approximately 3.17 terabytes (TB) of storage. VA conducts monthly enterprise scanning and daily on-demand scans supporting Authorization to Operate (ATO) activities. The current solution assesses at least 1,700 multi-vendor enterprise database targets within a 3-week period each month without adversely affecting the performance or availability of active ATO scanning. Database owners establish authorized scan windows and operational restrictions. The database inventory in the Draft PWS reflects VA s current environment and may change during the contract period. description: SPECIAL NOTICE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is issuing this special notice to announce an upcoming competition for a design and construction solicitation for the US Space Force (USSF) Integration Facility, F/10852 using Progressive Design-Build under 10 USC �2808a Other Transaction Authority for Construction. This notice is for informational and planning purposes to allow interested parties to prepare for and provide feedback prior to the official solicitation release. I. INDUSTRY DAY USACE intends to conduct an Industry Day on 03 December 2026 at 0900 Eastern Time to provide an overview of the project, acquisition strategy, and anticipated requirements. This event will provide interested parties with an opportunity to gain additional insight into the project and proposed PDB under an OT (non-FAR-based) framework. A notional acquisition schedule will be shared. Interested parties are encouraged to ask questions and provide input in advance of the official Request for Qualifications (RFQ) release. General questions will be permitted during the Industry Day; however, all discussions and responses provided during the event are considered unofficial and are for informational purposes only. Statements made during the Industry Day do not constitute commitment, authorization, or binding guidance related to the future RFQ. Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) will be accepted and addressed following the release of RFQ. II. LOCATION Industry Day Presentation location: Hope Hotel, 10823 Chidlaw Rd # A, Dayton, OH 45433 III. PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: US Space Force (USSF) Integration Facility, F/10852 Location: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), OH NAICS Code: 236220 Total Program Funding: $394,000,000.00 IV. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The USSF Integration Facility is a newly programmed mission at Wright-Patterson Air Force WPAFB, Ohio. This classified and contiguous operations area ultimately supports USSF�s mission to secure our Nation�s interest in, from, and to space as well as support across the Defense the Intelligence Enterprise. The new facility is situated adjacent to Building F/10854 to enable collaboration with partners and thus requires strict coordination for future utility access, physical security and logistics. Construction is broken into distinct agreement phases under the Progressive Design-Build (PDB) framework. Phase 1 (Design & Pre-Construction): This Phase is structured to collaboratively advance the facility design from initial concepts to 65% design maturity, perform detailed constructability reviews, conduct transparent open-book cost estimating, identify and mitigate complex interface risks, and validate the overall space programming. Pre-construction services will establish a baseline cost and allow for early design and potential separate authorization of long-lead procurement items. Phase 2 (Final Design and Construction): This Phase will include the completion of final design documents (95% and 100% Certified Final), fast-tracking capabilities, and all physical construction activities, including structural, interior finishes, specialized secure controlled space, redundant systems commissioning, and final security accreditation. Phase 2 will also include comprehensive site work, utility distribution integration, and connection into the active Building F/10854. Phase 2 covers construction of the multi-floor, approximately 333,700 SF secure USSF Integration Facility, including the physical connection to active Building F/10854, the integration of high-efficiency HVAC networks, a backup generator facility, high-security electrical switchgear, and the buildout of specialized controlled space. The Government will use available concept design information, programmed requirements, and initial planning data as the initial technical baseline. During Phase 1, the selected Design-Builder will validate the baseline and may recommend refinements; any material deviation from the Government�s baseline will require Government review and approval. The scope generally encompasses the following critical lines of effort: Critical Infrastructure and Utilities: Installation of high-efficiency mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems designed for 24/7 continuous operation, electrical tie-ins to centralized utilities, replacement of two existing end-of-life generators with new, Lightning Protection Systems (LPS), and addressable fire protection networks. Secure Facilities: Turnkey design, construction, and Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) accreditation of highly classified controlled space built to stringent ICD 705, IC Tech Spec, and Telecommunictaions Electronics Material Protected from Emanating Spurious Tranmission (TEMPEST) shielding standards to ensure complete physical, visual, and acoustic isolation. New Construction, Envelope, and Physical Connection: Construction of a new structural frame with metal panels and pre-cast exterior walls, establishing a secure thermal wall envelope, executing the physical and utility connection to adjacent operational Building F/10854, and conducting all associated site work, paving, and access control infrastructure. V. ACQUISITION STRATEGY - PRE-AWARD The USACE will use a streamlined competitive selection process: Step 1 �RFQ: Interested parties will submit a Statement of Qualifications (SOQ). Following evaluation of the qualification packages, the Government intends to short-list a target of three (3) of the highest qualified Design-Builders to proceed to Step 2. Step 2 � Pitches: Selected Companies will participate in pitch presentations. One company will be selected as the Design-Build team for award of the initial design and preconstruction services with a modification for design completion and construction award. Step 3 � Exclusive Negotiation: Based on pitch evaluations, the Government will select one Design-Builder to enter exclusive negotiations. VI. ACQUSITION STRATEGY � AWARD The agreement will be awarded to the most qualified progressive design-build entity (PDBE) to provide design development, preconstruction services, and construction. Post-award Phase 1 of PDB includes Design and Pre-construction services and Post-award Phase 2 includes the final design and construction. The agreement will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). The FFP for successive design and construction milestones will be agreed to as the design progresses and funds are available. VII. VIRTUAL PARTICIPATION OPPORTUNITY: For those who are unable to attend the Industry Day event in person, the Louisville District will also make the event available via Microsoft Teams. The details related to the MS Teams event are provided below: Microsoft Teams Meeting Join: https://dod.teams.microsoft.us/meet/993610255621?p=yaQ28DL3lmCC9Nap5C Meeting ID: 993 610 255 621 Passcode: Y6sB764r VIII. KEY SECURITY REQUIREMENTS This project will require the selected contractor and its subcontractor(s) to process, store, or transmit CUI and Federal Contract Information (FCI). In accordance with the CMMC program (32 CFR part 170) and USACE policy (including Alert 26-HQ-010, Rev1), CMMC Level 2 (Self) will be a mandatory prerequisite prior to award. Offerors must have an active SAM registration and a current, verified BASIC confidence level assessment (or higher) posted in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) in accordance with NIST SP 800-171. NOTE: An offeror will not be eligible for award if they do not possess the required CMMC status posted in SPRS prior to award. IX. CLOSING STATEMENT All interested parties should monitor the official solicitation announcement, which will provide complete details and submission instructions. Draft documents may be provided at a future date for feedback and informational purposes only and are subject to change upon issuance of the formal solicitation.

title: DA10--Office of Information & Technology Enterprise Database Vulnerability Scanning Solution
description: Request for Information 36C10B27Q0010 Page 2 of 2 Request for Information 36C10B27Q0010 Enterprise Database Vulnerability Scanning Solution INTRODUCTION This is a Request for Information (RFI) notice for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation, or a Request for Proposal. Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products described in this notice. Your response to this RFI notice will be treated only as information for the Government to consider. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI notice. This RFI notice does not constitute a solicitation for quotes/proposals or the authority to enter negotiations to award a contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition sensitive information contained in their response. The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI notice. Not responding to this RFI notice does not preclude participation in any future solicitation should one be issued. Any Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) or Veteran-owned small businesses (VOSBs) responding to this RFI notice must include their intent and ability to meet set-aside requirements for performance of this effort in accordance with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 852.219-73 or 852.219-74, VA Notice of Total Set-Aside for SDVOSB or VOSB respectively. Specifically, the requirement for at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing or 50% of the services be performed by yourself and/or other eligible and Small Business Administration verified SDVOSB/VOSB concerns; and certification from the Small Business Administration (VetCert). It is requested that all companies interested in participating in this RFI please note their interest and provide indication of their respective capabilities to perform the potential effort, as described in the paragraphs below and the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) Description. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI notice is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. VA reserves the right to not respond to any, all, or select responses or materials submitted. All requirements identified herein are subject to change at any time. The purpose of this RFI notice is for planning purposes, to identify market information and qualified contractors who are able to meet VA s requirement for Enterprise Database Vulnerability Scanning Solution. Any information provided in response to this RFI notice may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy and Performance Work Statement, as well as determining any set-aside decisions. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541519, Other Computer Related Services, with a size standard of 34 Million. Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in response to this RFI notice. Responses shall be as complete and informative as possible. It is the responsibility of interested parties to monitor this site for updates and/or additional information pertaining to this requirement. BACKGROUND: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information and Technology, Cybersecurity Operations Center (CSOC), requires an enterprise database vulnerability scanning solution to support recurring security assessments and Authorization to Operate (ATO) activities. VA currently uses LevelBlue Trustwave DbProtect across four production environments and one development environment. The existing capability includes centralized management, distributed scanning, vulnerability assessment content, reporting and analytics, and supporting repository and data-processing functions. Scanning components operate on premises and within VA Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft Azure environments. Management, reporting, and repository functions are hosted on premises. The current repository retains 12 months of scan information and uses approximately 3.17 terabytes (TB) of storage. VA conducts monthly enterprise scanning and daily on-demand scans supporting Authorization to Operate (ATO) activities. The current solution assesses at least 1,700 multi-vendor enterprise database targets within a 3-week period each month without adversely affecting the performance or availability of active ATO scanning. Database owners establish authorized scan windows and operational restrictions. The database inventory in the Draft PWS reflects VA s current environment and may change during the contract period. VA may add database types supported by the proposed solution, including those supported through standard product updates, during the base period or any exercised option period. Support for these additional database types shall be included at no additional cost to the Government, provided the total number of database assets remains within the enterprise licensed capacity required by the Draft PWS. The Contractor shall identify any database-specific licensing restrictions or additional charges in its proposal. If interested and capable of providing for this requirement, please see the Response Instructions and Submission Instruction sections below. title: Progressive Design-Build (PDB) - RENOVATE HQ AFMC B/10262 PH 2 at WPAFB
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is issuing this special notice to announce an upcoming competition for a construction solicitation for the Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC) Headquarters (HQ) Renovation, Building 10262, utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The anticipated delivery method is Progressive Design-Build (PDB). This notice is for informational and planning purposes. INDUSTRY DAY USACE intends to conduct an Industry Day on 03 December 2026 at 0900 Eastern Time to provide an overview of the project, acquisition strategy, and anticipated requirements. This event will provide interested parties with an opportunity to gain additional insight into the project and proposed PDB under an OT (non-FAR-based) framework. A notional acquisition schedule will be shared. Interested parties are encouraged to ask questions and provide input in advance of the official Request for Qualifications (RFQ) release. General questions will be permitted during the Industry Day; however, all discussions and responses provided during the event are considered unofficial and are for informational purposes only. Statements made during the Industry Day do not constitute commitment, authorization, or binding guidance related to the future RFQ. Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) will be accepted and addressed following the release of RFQ. LOCATION Industry Day Presentation location: Hope Hotel, 10823 Chidlaw Rd # A, Dayton, OH 45433 PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: Renovate Headquarters (HQ) Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC), Building 10262, Phase 2 Construction Location: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), OH Agency: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville District NAICS Code: 236220 PROJECT DESCRIPTION This acquisition will deliver the design and construction for the progressive design-build phased renovation of Building 10262, AFMC HQ, at WPAFB, OH. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary equipment, materials, labor, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver a fully functional, modernized headquarters facility while supporting ongoing occupied command operations. Key features of the project may include: Facility Renewal, Envelope, and Interior Renovation: Replacement of the Building 10262 roof and related envelope work, comprehensive interior renovation and finishes of the entire second floor, designated basement areas, required building repairs, and hazardous-material abatement. Critical Infrastructure Overhaul: Modernization and replacement of affected mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), electric-power, telecommunications, fire-protection, fire-alarm, and life-safety systems necessary to support the renovated areas. Secure Facilities & Specialized Spaces: Turnkey design, construction, and Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) accreditation of Special Access Program (SAP) and Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) spaces compliant with ICD 705 / IC Tech Spec and DoDM 5205.07 Vol 3 standards (including designated basement areas). Occupied Facility Logistics & Continuity: Construction sequencing, utility/system outage planning, temporary bypass systems, controlled access, and strict coordination to maintain uninterrupted global command operations supporting approximately 4,000 personnel. ACQUISITION STRATEGY � PRE-AWARD USACE � Louisville District will use a streamlined competitive selection process: Step 1 � RFQ: Interested parties will submit a Statement of Qualifications (SOQ). Following evaluation of the qualification packages, the Government intends to short-list a target of three (3) of the highest qualified Design-Builders to proceed to Step 2. Step 2 � Pitch Presentations: Short-listed firms must attend a mandatory site visit at WPAFB, OH during pitch preparation, followed by live, interactive presentations. Problem-solving, technical approach, risk management, and team chemistry will be evaluated by the Government. Step 3 � Exclusive Negotiation: Based on pitch evaluations, the Government will select one Design-Builder to enter exclusive negotiations. All interested parties should monitor the official solicitation announcement, which will provide complete details and submission instructions. Draft documents may be provided at a future date for feedback and informational purposes only and are subject to change upon issuance of the formal project RFQ. Virtual Participation Opportunity: For those who are unable to attend the Industry Day event in person, the Louisville District will also make the event available via Microsoft Teams. The details related to the MS Teams event are provided below: Microsoft Teams Meeting Join: https://dod.teams.microsoft.us/meet/993610255621?p=yaQ28DL3lmCC9Nap5C Meeting ID: 993 610 255 621 Passcode: Y6sB764r This is a combined Industry Day for AFMC and United States Space Force (USSF).

title: France – Technical assistance services – Prestations d'assistance technique "mission d'animateur sécurité et environnement", pour le compte du CEA, centre de Valduc
description: Les prestations comprennent plusieurs activités d'assistance à l'exploitation et à la sécurité de certaines installations du CEA Centre de Valduc (avec une partie des bâtiments à caractère industriel et nucléaire) telles que : - des diagnostics et analyses de sécurité (compléter des autorisations d'intervention, des convocations et plans de prévention, rédaction de rapports de contrôle, de déroulement d'opération, d'accident de travail, etc), - des analyses/évaluations des risques (création de mode opératoire, rédaction de bilan de sécurité, mise à jour de dossiers d'évaluation des risques, etc), - des actions de prévention (création et mise à jour de consigne de sécurité, mise à jour de fiches d'unité de travail, planification des accueils sécurité, création de divers supports de présentation, mise à jour des divers plans de sécurité, rédaction de comptes-rendus, etc), - de la gestion des produits chimiques (inventaire et mise à jour des classeurs de fiches de données de sécurité).

title: Saltash Guildhall Internal Works
description: Saltash Town Council is seeking tenders from suitably qualified contractors for internal remodelling works at the Guildhall, Lower Fore Street, Saltash. The project comprises refurbishment and adaptation works to support revised council operations and meeting functions, including: Manufacture and installation of bespoke horseshoe-shaped council chamber desking accommodating approximately 20 members/users. Supply and installation of audio visual equipment to support hybrid meetings, Microsoft Teams connectivity, microphones, displays, speakers and associated control systems. Installation of an assisted listening system. Electrical alterations and new power and data infrastructure within the First Floor Long Room. Electrical and data alterations within the Ground Floor Council Chamber. Electrical and data alterations within the Clerk's Office. Heating alterations including replacement radiators within the Council Chamber. Supply and installation of acoustic underlay and new carpet finishes within the First Floor Long Room. Associated commissioning, testing, certification, training and making good. The works will be undertaken within an occupied civic building and contractors must maintain safe operation of the premises throughout the contract period.

title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source KeyTrak Maintenance
description: This is a NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT in accordance with: � FAR 6.103-1 and Title 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) � 3204(a)(1) ("Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements"); � FAR Subpart 12.2 / FAR 12.201-1 ("Simplified Procedures for Commercial Products and Commercial Services"); and The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) Fort Benning, on behalf of the Directorate of Training Sustainment (DOTS), intends to negotiate and award a sole-source, Firm-Fixed-Price purchase order/contract to: � Contractor: KEY-TECH SALES & SERVICES, LLC The Directorate of Training Sustainment (DOTS) has an immediate and continuous operational requirement for specialized preventative maintenance, corrective diagnostic repair, micro-controller calibration, and hardware upkeep for its existing inventory of four (4) KeyTrak electronic key storage systems deployed across Fort Benning. The scope of work encompasses: � Third-Party Technical Maintenance & Emergency Repair: Performance of scheduled operational maintenance, routine calibrations, and on-call corrective repairs to maintain full mechanical and electronic operability of the four KeyTrak key storage enclosures. � Component Replacement & Hardware Support: Sourcing and installation of compatible replacement components, including locking solenoids, power distribution modules, micro-controller boards, and key-tag tracking interfaces to prevent system failure. � Preservation of Chain-of-Custody & Physical Security Safeguards: Ensuring continuous, zero-downtime key-control management to maintain audit tracking and physical security protocols for government fleet vehicles, arms/ammunition supply areas, and secured facilities across the installation. Based on technical market analysis, KEY-TECH SALES & SERVICES, LLC is currently the sole identified commercial provider possessing the requisite diagnostic tooling, technician proficiency, and supply chain access for KeyTrak-compatible replacement components necessary to maintain these four installed units without mission failure. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes or proposals. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based upon responses received is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. Any alternative contractor proposing to satisfy this requirement must demonstrate independent technical capability, technician experience, and verified access to KeyTrak-compatible replacement parts and diagnostic equipment without causing unacceptable operational downtime. Replacing the existing installed KeyTrak infrastructure with an entirely new key control platform would cause the Government substantial duplication of unrecoverable costs (including hardware procurement, facility mounting, network reconfiguration, and disposal) alongside severe disruption to mission operations. Interested organizations that believe they possess the technical capability and component supply access to satisfy this requirement without unacceptable delay or substantial duplication of cost may submit a technical capability statement. Responses must include the following information: 1. Company Name and Physical Address. 2. Technical Capability Statement demonstrating independent technical expertise, diagnostic methodology, and past performance maintaining and repairing KeyTrak electronic key storage systems. 3. Supply Chain Verification detailing access to reliable replacement hardware and components (e.g., locking solenoids, micro-controllers, circuit boards, and key tags) compatible with KeyTrak units. 4. SAM CAGE Code and Unique Entity ID (UEI). 5. Point of Contact Information (Name, title, telephone number, and official corporate email address). 6. Business Size Status in relation to NAICS code 561621 / PSC J063. All inquiries and capability responses must be submitted via email. No telephone inquiries or verbal requests will be accepted. Notice of Intent Contacts: � Contract Specialist: Aaliyah Giadoo Email: Aaliyah.c.giadoo.civ@army.mil � Contracting Officer: Stacia Rivers Email: Stacia.m.rivers.civ@army.mil

title: Annual Subscription to The American Registry for Internet Numbers (ARIN)
description: This is a SOLE SOURCE Special Notice in support of a planned SOLE-SOURCE acquisition�by the Office of the Secretary of Transportation, on behalf of Federal Highway Administration. This office plans to purchase an annual subscription to The American Registry for Internet Numbers (ARIN) in the amount of $17,640 for 12 months. The Department of Transportation (DOT) makes this Brand Name Justification pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1: "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements" following RFO/FAR 6.104-1 format listed below. (a) At a minimum, each justification must include the following information: (1) Identification of the agency and the contracting activity, and specific identification of the document as a �Justification for other than full and open competition.� This document is the Justification for other than full and open competition for the Department of Transportation (DOT) Office of the Chief Digital & Information Officer (OCDIO) for a firm-fixed price, sole source award to the American Registry for Internet Numbers (ARIN). (2) Nature and/or description of the action being approved. This requirement will be for the purchase of the ARIN annual subscription. ARIN is the non-profit organization responsible for managing and assigning official IP (Internet Protocol) addresses and Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) in our region across the United States, Canada, and many Caribbean and North Atlantic islands. Without this active registration, the agency cannot legally control, expand, or route its Internet IP addresses�the foundational visual "street addresses" that allow internal networks, external services, public portals, and secure communications to connect across the Internet. (3) A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency's needs (including the estimated value). This procurement effort will enable the OCDIO to renew the annual ARIN subscription. This subscription is renewed annually for 12 months at a time and is required for as long as DOT maintains a webpage. The estimated value of this requirement is $17,640 for a period of performance from 10/31/2026 to 10/30/2027. (4) An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition. The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition for this contract is the Federal Acquisition Regulation FAR 6.103-1: "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements". (5) A demonstration that the proposed contractor's unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires using the authority cited. The service is provided directly by ARIN and does not have any resellers. DOT must award to ARIN because they are the only entity that provides the service to govern IP addresses. No other company provides this service. This is an IT networking standard and there is no other company or reseller that can offer the same service. Google, Gemini, and NASA SEWP were used to come to this conclusion. We put out a solicitation on NASA SEWP in October 2026 that did not return any quotes due to there being no resellers. ARIN also confirmed that they have no resellers and no one else can offer the service they provide. (6) A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as possible, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by part 5 and, if not, which exception under part 5 applies. We put out a solicitation on NASA SEWP in October 2026 that did not return any quotes due to there being no resellers. The contracting officer also posted an RFQ on NASA SEWP in November 2026 that yielded the same results. Only one offer can be made, and the source is directly from ARIN. Therefore, this Sole Source Special Notice numbered 693JK427Q600001, as published by DOT contracting officer Melinda Riddick in the SAM.gov website, constitutes the needed notice contemplated in RFO/FAR 5.201. (7) A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable. The cost will be fair and reasonable as there is only one quoted price by ARIN and service costs are listed publicly based on the size of the business requiring the service. There is no other cost to compare it with, and this is the only cost possible for this service. (8) The market research conducted (see part 10), and the results or a statement of the reason market research was not conducted. OCDIO posted a solicitation on NASA SEWP in October 2026 that did not return any quotes due to there being no resellers. The contracting officer also posted an RFQ on NASA SEWP in November 2026 that yielded the same results. Only one offer can be made, and the source is directly from ARIN. (9) Any other facts supporting use other than full and open competition, such as: The American Registry for Internet Numbers (ARIN) is the non-profit organization responsible for managing and assigning official IP (Internet Protocol) addresses and Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) in our region. There are no competitors or resellers for this service. The ARIN Annual Registration Services Plan is mission critical because it maintains the agency�s official ownership, registration, and active routing rights for its entire digital infrastructure. (i) When 6.103-1 is cited for follow-on acquisitions as described in 6.103-1(c)(2), an estimate of the cost to the Government that would be duplicated and how the estimate was derived. The estimate was derived from a price quote submitted by ARIN to renewal the annual subscription. (ii) When 6.103-2 is cited, data, estimated cost, or other rationale as to whether and how much the Government would be harmed. ARIN is the exclusive Regional Internet Registry (RIR) for North America and the only entity authorized to maintain the registration and global routing validity of the agency's assigned IP addresses and Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs). Without this active registration, the agency cannot legally control, expand, or route its Internet IP addresses�the foundational visual "street addresses" that allow internal networks, external services, public portals, and secure communications to connect across the Internet. Based on this assessment, ARIN is essential to the Government�s requirements, and no other service or product can meet or can be modified to meet the agency�s needs. If the ARIN Annual Fee for Registration Services Plan is not procured the following consequences may occur: Complete Disruption of Online Public Services: The agency risks losing the rights to its registered IP addresses. Over time, these addresses could be reclaimed or deregistered, causing public-facing portals, citizen services, applications, and official websites to become completely unreachable on the Internet. Failure of Internal Infrastructure and Remote Operations: Critical agency networks, secure VPN access for staff, remote work capabilities, and cloud integrations rely on ARIN-registered routing records. Loss of service would prevent employees from securely connecting to core tools, databases, and operations. Severe Cybersecurity and Fraud Risks: Active ARIN registration ensures that our IP addresses are authenticated (via DNSSEC and RPKI protocols). If registration lapses, cybercriminals could hijack the agency's unmanaged IP space, launch phishing campaigns using our address footprint, or intercept agency communications. Halting of Infrastructure Upgrades: Without an active registration plan, the agency cannot request additional IP address allocations, transfer network resources, or update routing records necessary for network expansions and technology modernizations. (11) A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisition of the supplies or services required. description: Lake Baldwin VA Clinic, FL EUL Request for Expressions of Interest 1 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST ENHANCED-USE LEASE DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITY Orlando Healthcare System Veterans Integrated Service Network 08 (VISN 08) Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic - Orlando, FL Notice This advertisement is a notice of a potential opportunity. This Request for Expressions of Interest (the advertisement ) is not a solicitation for offers, nor is it a request for proposals. Respondents are advised that the Government assumes no responsibility to award an Enhanced-Use Lease (EUL) based upon responses to this advertisement. This Sources Sought Notice is to identify potential sources for information and planning purposes only and is not intended to pre-qualify or disqualify any potential Respondents. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to conduct market research to determine if there are responsible and qualified entities interested in redeveloping the assets described in Section III and if yes, what potential reuse options exist. The information gained from this Sources Sought will be used to assist the Government in determining if this development opportunity can be competitive and/or a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) Set-Aside. The Government will use this information to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement and to inform related asset management decision-making. The Government requests that interested parties respond to this Notice with the specific information requested in Section V of this Notice and identify their small business status. VA is particularly interested in SDVOSB/VOSB respondents capabilities to perform a minimum of 51% of the development opportunity described in this Notice. Developers responding to this market research should be aware that responding to this advertisement may not ensure that they qualify for any underlying future solicitation or contract award. Responding to this Sources Sought Notice is NOT a prerequisite to respond to any future subsequent solicitations. The Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this Sources Sought. The Government cannot provide any warranty, expressed or implied, as to the accuracy, reliability or completeness of the information contained in this Notice. Overview and Objectives The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), under its Enhanced-Use Leasing (EUL) authority (38 U.S.C. §§ 8161- 8169, as amended), is seeking expressions of interest from qualified developers, including SDVOSBs and VOSBs, to serve as a Developer for purposes of developing supportive housing or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans (e.g., general affordable housing, skilled nursing facilities, technical job training centers, research facilities, mixed-use, other). VA s EUL authority allows VA to outlease land and improvements to selected developers (i.e., Lessees) to provide housing and/or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program. An EUL is a long-term ground lease of underutilized VA-owned land or buildings to a non-federal entity (Developer). Under the EUL program, the Developer secures a long-term leasehold interest with VA for the subject property. This deal structure enables developers to finance, design, develop, renovate/construct, operate, and maintain improvements on VA property to directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. The objective of this development opportunity is to repurpose assets at the Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic under VA s EUL Program to the benefit of Veterans. Respondents should consider the following as they formulate responses to this Notice: Lease-back by VA or other Federal government entities is not permissible, and financing cannot reflect a lease-back arrangement. The PACT Act does not nullify 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(5), which states, "The terms of an enhanced-use lease may not provide for any acquisition, contract, demonstration, exchange, grant, incentive, procurement, sale, other transaction authority, service agreement, use agreement, lease, or lease-back by the Secretary or Federal Government. VA may only receive cash consideration for ground lease rent in an EUL (per 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(B)). This means VA cannot receive any in-kind consideration or free/discounted services as part of a new EUL agreement. However, projects may provide free or discounted services to individual Veterans or Veteran Service Organizations, and the Secretary may enter into an EUL without receiving consideration per U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(C). Additional information on the VA s EUL program and sample EUL projects may be obtained at: http://www.va.gov/assetmanagement/. Development Scope The intent of this Notice is to determine if there are experienced developers, including SDVOSB or VOSB developers, that can develop the subject assets in accordance with VA s EUL authority. The Developer would undertake all necessary investigative activities to develop the selected assets at the Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic campus. VA is especially interested in development of supportive housing but will also consider other uses that benefit Veterans. The assets that may be redeveloped by a Developer include, but are not limited to, the following interconnected buildings (with current use in parentheses): Building 519 (Domiciliary) Building 519a (Dining / education space in the first floor courtyard) Building 520 (Domiciliary) Building 520a (Domiciliary reception / elevator space in Northwest corner of the interconnected buildings) Building 521 (Domiciliary) Building 522 (Domiciliary) Please see Attachment A for a map of the Campus and Attachment B for asset information and photos. Lake Baldwin VA Clinic Background The Lake Baldwin VA Clinic in Orlando, Florida, traces its origins to a former U.S. Navy facility. In 1968, the Navy took over an Air Force hospital in the Lake Baldwin neighborhood, opening it as Naval Hospital Orlando. By 1995, the Navy closed Naval Hospital Orlando as part of broader base closures. The facility was then transferred to VA and rebranded as the Lake Baldwin VA Clinic. VA originally used the site as part of its outpatient and transitional care network, with some portions serving as labs, treatment spaces, and administrative offices. The 46-acre campus is located at 5201 Raymond Street, Orlando, FL 32803. The Lake Baldwin outpatient clinic offers urgent care, primary care, surgery, and specialty health services, including mental health care, laboratory services, vision care (optometry), pain management, prosthetics, physical therapy, nutrition services, homeless Veteran care, women Veteran care, and more. Financial wherewithal required to successfully develop the proposed use(s) with associated amenities (if applicable); and, Securing public and private financing for projects comparable to the proposed use(s) for the designated assets. For SDVOSB/VOSB developers, VA is seeking to confirm the Respondent s ability to perform a minimum of 51% of the development opportunity described in this Notice. title: W065--medical-grade oxygen cylinders/tanks
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Networking Contracting Office (NCO 01) located in Brockton, MA intends to enter into a sole source procurement, pursuant to the authority of FAR 6.302-1, with Airgas USA, LLC, for the following requirement: Statement of Work General: The contractor will provide delivery of all requirements for individual compressed gas cylinders/tanks to the locations listed in this document. Period of Performance: base year plus one option year Base year: January 1, 2027 - December 31, 2027 Option year one: January 1, 2028 December 31, 2028 Intended Use: To meet the needs for patients requiring oxygen therapy during transport to different locations of the Boston VA Healthcare System within the facilities. The requirement of the following are estimated amount of each specific size, type of material the cylinder is manufactured of, cylinders with integrated regulators and handles. Integrated valve stem regulator with the aluminum cylinder are utilized throughout Boston Healthcare System. Boston VA Healthcare System requires that all of the hospital transport cylinders be light weight cylinders with integrated regulator with wide handle that is secured to the regulator that extends upward for ease of carrying. The integrated regulator must be able to deliver a flow rate of 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 15, 25 liters per minute flow. The regulator also must provide a 50 psi outlet port to connection to equipment if needed. Boston VA Healthcare System requires that of the hospital MR compatible transport cylinders be light weight cylinders with integrated regulator with wide handle that is secured to the regulator that extends upward for ease of carrying. The integrated regulator must be able to deliver a flow rate of 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 15, 25 liters per minute flow. The regulator also must provide a 50 psi outlet port to connection to equipment if needed. Boston VA Healthcare System requires that all H cylinders are made of Steel with the Diameter Index Safety System. These cylinders are utilized for Emergency Back Up during an oxygen failure or shut down. Place of Performance: West Roxbury VA Medical Center 1400 VFW Pkwy, West Roxbury, MA 02132 Jamaica Plain VA Medical Center 150 South Huntington Ave, Boston, MA 02130 Brockton VA Medical Center 940 Belmont St Brockton, MA 02301 Day and Hours of Operation: West Roxbury VA Medical Center: M-F 0800-1600 or after regular duty hours by calling the respiratory care department for access. Jamaica Plain VA Medical Center: M-F 0800-1600 Brockton VA Medical Center: M-F 0800-1600 Performance Requirements: The contractor must be able to supply the facilities listed above with the medical grade compressed gases listed in Section 8 weekly. Specifically- deliveries are to be made to West Roxbury campus every Monday and Thursday without fail excluding holidays at which point a needs assessment will be completed and the company will push delivery to the next business day. Deliveries will be made twice per week at the Jamaica Plain campus every Monday and Thursday following the same protocol as West Roxbury. Deliveries will be made twice per week at the Brockton campus following same scheduling and protocol as West Roxbury. The contractor will respond to emergency calls within 2 hours. The contractor shall respond to non-emergency call within 24 hours or the next business day. The contractor shall repair all minor cylinder leaks detected and provide a full report of leak tests and any leaks repaired to the Contracting Officer s Representative (COR). Patient and occupation safety require that all tanks meet all regulatory guidelines and the tanks and regulators allow continuous oxygen flow between regulator settings. Safety features include: Oxygen flow that does not stop if the regulator is placed between two numbers. Integrated valve and regulator that is built into tank and doesn t need to be installed by staff. Single valve tank. No tanks with two valves, this is a human factor safety risk. National Center for Patient Safety discourages any two valve tanks. Rupture disk relief valve. 50 PSI DISS outlet that delivers up to 200 lpm if needed for mechanical ventilator device. Invoices: Invoicing is required to be submitted per delivery. Payment will be made upon receipt of a properly prepared detailed invoice, prepared by the contractor, validated by the contracting officer s representative (COR) and submitted. A properly prepared invoice will contain: Invoice number and date Contractor s name and address Contract number Accurate purchase order number Itemized supply or service provider Total amount due Medical Gases and Supplies to be Provided: West Roxbury Location Furnish and maintain 3429 E cylinder made of aluminum with integrated valve. Furnish and maintain 483 MRI safe E cylinder made of aluminum with integrated valve. Furnish and maintain 43 H cylinder made of steel using DISS system. Jamaica Plain Location Furnish and maintain 3429 E cylinder made of aluminum with integrated valve. Furnish and maintain 33 H cylinder made of steel using DISS system Brockton Location Furnish and maintain 3429 E cylinder made of aluminum with integrated valve Furnish and maintain 33 H cylinder made of steel using DISS system The NAICS code for this requirement is 532490. Airgas USA, LLC is the only vendor capable of providing the required services as they presently have liquid oxygen tanks located at all three(3) facilities within the Boston Healthcare System; they also have backup reserves at these facilities (3 in Brockton, 1 in West Roxbury, 1 at JP). The station tanks are owned by Airgas USA, LLC and proprietary to their oxygen supply. Due to liability issues, it is not permissible or legal for a contractor other than Airgas to fill or maintain the tanks owned by Airgas. Airgas provides annual inspections and preventative maintenance on the station tanks at no additional cost to the government and provides reports on operation and condition to each facility. If the new requirement were to be awarded to another company, the existing station tanks would need to be removed from each VA Facility. The cost of removal alone is estimated by the incumbent contractor to be upwards of $45,000.00 which does not include installation of new tanks. If another vendor was awarded this requirement, the supplier of the oxygen itself would need to change as Airgas will fill and maintain tanks owned only by Airgas. The removal and replacement of station tanks would be cost prohibitive to the amount of funding allocated by the VA Boston Healthcare System for this service, would require numerous labor hours across multiple VA departments to coordinate, supervise, receive and test the replacement and would create a disruption in the provision of bulk oxygen to the facility. The lapse of medical gasses to the Boston Healthcare System would require the coordination of multiple medical departments within each facility to ensure patient care is not impacted. Installing out a new system would impinge clinical service as alternative delivery sources would have to be established for the period of system change out. The tanks currently are meeting current demands and meet all the demands of the Boston VA health care needs. Concrete pads currently in place would have to be reconfigured and additional contracts would need to be in place with construction in order to have this done. The current plumbing situation would have to be replaced and reconfigured to meet specs of new tanks. This also would incur additional costs with a new service contract. The Boston VA Healthcare system would have to supply alternative source of oxygen during all above and would necessitate great cost for supplies, labor and other variable costs.
