title: R799--Lake Baldwin EUL Development Opportunity Sources Sought COR: Dustin Koonce
description: Lake Baldwin VA Clinic, FL EUL Request for Expressions of Interest 1 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST ENHANCED-USE LEASE DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITY Orlando Healthcare System Veterans Integrated Service Network 08 (VISN 08) Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic - Orlando, FL Notice This advertisement is a notice of a potential opportunity. This Request for Expressions of Interest (the advertisement ) is not a solicitation for offers, nor is it a request for proposals. Respondents are advised that the Government assumes no responsibility to award an Enhanced-Use Lease (EUL) based upon responses to this advertisement. This Sources Sought Notice is to identify potential sources for information and planning purposes only and is not intended to pre-qualify or disqualify any potential Respondents. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to conduct market research to determine if there are responsible and qualified entities interested in redeveloping the assets described in Section III and if yes, what potential reuse options exist. The information gained from this Sources Sought will be used to assist the Government in determining if this development opportunity can be competitive and/or a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) Set-Aside. The Government will use this information to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement and to inform related asset management decision-making. The Government requests that interested parties respond to this Notice with the specific information requested in Section V of this Notice and identify their small business status. VA is particularly interested in SDVOSB/VOSB respondents capabilities to perform a minimum of 51% of the development opportunity described in this Notice. Developers responding to this market research should be aware that responding to this advertisement may not ensure that they qualify for any underlying future solicitation or contract award. Responding to this Sources Sought Notice is NOT a prerequisite to respond to any future subsequent solicitations. The Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this Sources Sought. The Government cannot provide any warranty, expressed or implied, as to the accuracy, reliability or completeness of the information contained in this Notice. Overview and Objectives The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), under its Enhanced-Use Leasing (EUL) authority (38 U.S.C. §§ 8161- 8169, as amended), is seeking expressions of interest from qualified developers, including SDVOSBs and VOSBs, to serve as a Developer for purposes of developing supportive housing or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans (e.g., general affordable housing, skilled nursing facilities, technical job training centers, research facilities, mixed-use, other). VA s EUL authority allows VA to outlease land and improvements to selected developers (i.e., Lessees) to provide housing and/or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program. An EUL is a long-term ground lease of underutilized VA-owned land or buildings to a non-federal entity (Developer). Under the EUL program, the Developer secures a long-term leasehold interest with VA for the subject property. This deal structure enables developers to finance, design, develop, renovate/construct, operate, and maintain improvements on VA property to directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. The objective of this development opportunity is to repurpose assets at the Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic under VA s EUL Program to the benefit of Veterans. Respondents should consider the following as they formulate responses to this Notice: Lease-back by VA or other Federal government entities is not permissible, and financing cannot reflect a lease-back arrangement. The PACT Act does not nullify 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(5), which states, "The terms of an enhanced-use lease may not provide for any acquisition, contract, demonstration, exchange, grant, incentive, procurement, sale, other transaction authority, service agreement, use agreement, lease, or lease-back by the Secretary or Federal Government. VA may only receive cash consideration for ground lease rent in an EUL (per 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(B)). This means VA cannot receive any in-kind consideration or free/discounted services as part of a new EUL agreement. However, projects may provide free or discounted services to individual Veterans or Veteran Service Organizations, and the Secretary may enter into an EUL without receiving consideration per U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(C). Additional information on the VA s EUL program and sample EUL projects may be obtained at: http://www.va.gov/assetmanagement/. Development Scope The intent of this Notice is to determine if there are experienced developers, including SDVOSB or VOSB developers, that can develop the subject assets in accordance with VA s EUL authority. The Developer would undertake all necessary investigative activities to develop the selected assets at the Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic campus. VA is especially interested in development of supportive housing but will also consider other uses that benefit Veterans. The assets that may be redeveloped by a Developer include, but are not limited to, the following interconnected buildings (with current use in parentheses): Building 519 (Domiciliary) Building 519a (Dining / education space in the first floor courtyard) Building 520 (Domiciliary) Building 520a (Domiciliary reception / elevator space in Northwest corner of the interconnected buildings) Building 521 (Domiciliary) Building 522 (Domiciliary) Please see Attachment A for a map of the Campus and Attachment B for asset information and photos. Lake Baldwin VA Clinic Background The Lake Baldwin VA Clinic in Orlando, Florida, traces its origins to a former U.S. Navy facility. In 1968, the Navy took over an Air Force hospital in the Lake Baldwin neighborhood, opening it as Naval Hospital Orlando. By 1995, the Navy closed Naval Hospital Orlando as part of broader base closures. The facility was then transferred to VA and rebranded as the Lake Baldwin VA Clinic. VA originally used the site as part of its outpatient and transitional care network, with some portions serving as labs, treatment spaces, and administrative offices. The 46-acre campus is located at 5201 Raymond Street, Orlando, FL 32803. The Lake Baldwin outpatient clinic offers urgent care, primary care, surgery, and specialty health services, including mental health care, laboratory services, vision care (optometry), pain management, prosthetics, physical therapy, nutrition services, homeless Veteran care, women Veteran care, and more. title: 6810--501 - Dry Ice Base +4
description: The purpose of this amendment is to answer questions regarding Pre-solicitation Notice 36C26227Q0115. Q: Is 5/8 inch a strict nominal diameter, or is there an allowable tolerance? Would nominal 1/2-inch pellets be acceptable? A: 5/8 inch is preferred but 1/2 inch would be acceptable. No larger than 3/4 inch. Q: What documentation should offerors provide to demonstrate that the proposed container meets the stated specifications and the target of less than 8% sublimation loss per 24 hours? A: Manufacture documentation will be required. Q: The notice lists both 7:30 a.m. 3:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. 3:30 p.m. Mountain Time. Which window applies to the receiving dock at 2401 Centre Ave SE? A: 7:30 am 3:00 pm MT Q: Would the VA accept two insulated containers containing 300 lbs each, for a combined weekly delivery of 600 lbs, instead of a single container with a minimum capacity of 700 lbs? A: The weekly delivery must be at least 550lbs and no more than 600lbs in a single container. Q: Would the VA accept weekly deliveries on Thursdays or Fridays instead of Mondays, provided we consistently deliver the required 600 lbs? Thursday would be our preferred delivery day, subject to confirmation of our ability to maintain that schedule. A: Thursday/Friday delivery will lead to excess waste and will not be appropriate for the hospital s scheduled send-outs. Q: Could you confirm whether November 26, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Pacific is the deadline for responding to the pre-solicitation or for submitting a formal quote? Please also let us know where the solicitation and submission instructions will be available. A: The date and time, extended to Monday, November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Pacific Time, is the deadline for responding to the pre-solicitation notice and expressing interest in the requirement. It is not the deadline for submission of a formal quote. The Government intends to issue the solicitation directly to vendors determined capable of meeting the requirement based on: Vendors identified through market research. Vendors known to carry the required product. Vendors capable of meeting delivery requirements. Vendors that satisfy the socioeconomic requirement. Past performance. Price. Q: Should each annual CLIN be quoted as a single delivered price per pound that includes delivery, fuel, hazmat fees, and container exchange? A: Yes. Q: Will a supplier's weight ticket be sufficient to verify the 600-pound net delivery, or does the receiving team weigh it on site? A: Weight tickets will be sufficient. Q: Should the driver exchange containers at the dock or move them to a designated storage area? How should the driver handle any dry ice remaining in the previous container? A: Any remaining dry ice from previous deliveries will be transferred before exchanges, which will occur at the dock. Receiving personnel will move the deliveries to the storage area. Q: Does SBA's class waiver of the nonmanufacturer rule for industrial gases (NAICS 325120, PSC 6810) apply to this requirement, or must the dry ice be produced by a small business manufacturer? A: The nonmanufacturer rule will apply to this requirement. Q: May the contractor's supplier own the insulated storage containers and swap them at each weekly delivery? A: Yes. Q: Can invoicing occur weekly? A: Invoices will need to be submitted monthly, in arrears.

title: FWS - Pixley NWR Water Recirculation Design-Build
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes only solicitation. Offers are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service, Pixley National Wildlife Refuge provides 755 acres of wetland habitat for migratory waterfowl and other water birds and relies on three deep groundwater wells for irrigation and flooding. This project will improve water reuse and reduce groundwater pumping demands, particularly during drought years. The contractor shall design and construct a water recirculation system consisting of approximately 1.2 miles of PVC pipeline connecting the wetlands� lowest topographical point to the existing pipeline farther east. The system shall include a pump at this low point to move water upslope for recirculation and critical irrigation. description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Information Processing Techniques Office (IPTO) seeks information on research related to Formal Learning and Abstractions for System Heterogeneity (FLASH). description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a request for proposal. The National Institute of Health, Clinical Center (NIH-CC) intends to negotiate on an other than full and open competition basis with the following vendor: Rees Scientific. The period of performance is expected between December 1, 2026 and December 10, 2026 for installation, calibration, and certification of all wireless modules and probe. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source � SOFT COMPUTER CONSULTANTS INC
description: This is a notice of intent, not a request for a quotation. A solicitation document will not be issued and quotations will not be requested. This procurement is acquisition is to continue to obtain Soft software and hardware license and maintenance services for the IBM hardware and AIX operating system for servers that support the existing Laboratory Information System (LIS). Soft Computer Corporation (SCC) has been the incumbent since the initial install of the software and due to its proprietary nature they have performed the ongoing maintenance and support on the system. The current LIS software system is proprietary to SCC who developed it. SCC does not permit 3rd party maintenance and will not release their source code to other entities. As the LIS modules in the Clinical Center are currently handling large volumes of patient data and test and diagnostic results, it is absolutely imperative that there be no interruption in the ongoing operation/functioning of the existing system. Patient safety is of great concern if there is a system failure or interruption in service. Therefore it is critical that the system continues to be maintained by SCC who is the only source capable of providing the necessary maintenance, including making revisions to the source code as circumstances may dictate. Because the LIS helps support patient diagnosis and care activities, it is deemed a mission critical system for the Clinical Center. The proprietary status of the system to SCC clearly demonstrates that they are the only firm qualified to perform the required maintenance services. This acquisition is being conducted using policies unique to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 13 �Simplified Acquisition Procedures, Subpart 13.500 This subpart authorizes the use of simplified procedures for the acquisition of supplies and services in amounts greater than the simplified acquisition threshold but not exceeding $9 million ($15 million for acquisitions as described in 13.500(c)), including options, if the contracting officer reasonably expects, based on the nature of the supplies or services sought, and on market research, that offers will include only commercial products or commercial services. Contracting officers may use any simplified acquisition procedure in this part, subject to any specific dollar limitation applicable to the particular procedure. Contracts awarded using FAR Part 13-Simplified Acquisition Procedures are exempt from the requirements of FAR Part 6-Competition Requirements. Comments to this announcement, referencing this posting number, may be submitted to the NIH, Clinical Center, Office of Purchasing and Contracts, prior to the closing date specified in this announcement, to the attention of Ryssa Nix, Contract Specialist via email to Ryssa.nix@nih.gov by close date. title: Spain – Water-treatment chemicals – Suministro de reactivos para la potabilización del agua en las Estaciones de Tratamiento de Aguas Potables (ETAP) que gestiona Aguas de Córdoba-EMPROACSA mediante sistema dinámico de adquisición
description: Las diferentes Estaciones de Tratamiento de Agua Potable ETAP gestionadas por Aguas de Córdoba-EMPROACSA necesitan del suministro continuado de diferentes productos químicos a fin de garantizar el apropiado tratamiento y, por tanto, la salubridad del agua para poder cumplir con los parámetros exigidos por la normativa vigente para la potabilización del agua. Teniendo en cuenta la exhaustiva norma que regula la fabricación, transporte, descarga y dosificación de los productos empleados en la potabilización del agua de consumo humano y la necesidad permanente de suministro de tales productos, se hace necesaria la contratación de los mismos con empresas especializadas y que reúnan los requerimientos normativos exigidos para garantizar la salubridad del agua de consumo humano. La modalidad de contratación que se propone, a través de sistema dinámico de adquisición, nace de la necesidad de mejorar los tiempos de respuesta a determinadas necesidades de la organización.

description: VA is seeking sources that are able to provide full lifecycle sustainment and operational support, and any associated bug/fix development, and regulatory compliance services for the VA s existing Veterans Health Administration s VBECS, an FDA regulated Class II Medical Device Software product. description: This Sources Sought Notice is for Market Research ONLY to determine the availability, capability and interest of small business firms for a potential small business category type set-aside. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME as this is solely for Market Research. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential acquisition. The purpose of this notice is to obtain a snapshot of current market capabilities and gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following socioeconomic categories: Certified HUB Zone; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) and 8(a) small business concerns to perform database updates to increase the capabilities, usability, and stability of currently existing applications. Other than small business are encouraged to express interest and submit capability statements as well. Contractors� capabilities will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining an appropriate acquisition strategy to include whether this prospective action is appropriate to be set-aside for the small business community or should proceed as an unrestricted full and open acquisition. Other than small businesses are encouraged to respond to this NOTICE to provide a greater context of current market capabilities. However, per the Federal Acquisition Regulations, preference will be given to the small business categories as listed above. In determining the acquisition strategy, the Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Price order with a Period of Performance of five (5) years from date of award. An estimated solicitation date has not yet been determined. The NAICS Code is 562910, Environmental Remediation Services. The Size Standard in Number of Employees: 1,000 Employees. Product Service Code is B510. GENERAL SCOPE: Regulatory & Data Governance Regulatory Framework: This Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) site is governed by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in which the work must strictly adhere to the developed Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Remedial Investigation (RI) Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) which utilizes the Uniform Federal Policy for Quality Assurance Project Plans (UFP-QAPP). The Contractor must transmit all documents and data via Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS). All actions are dictated by the Federal Facilities Agreement (FFA) with the regulatory community. The Contractor will anticipate significant comments on products generated for this effort and must present technically competent PFAS subject matter experts to address and resolve comments suitable for public consumption per EPA Risk Communication guidelines. The Contractor must demonstrate past experience executing CERCLA work under an active FFA alongside USACE, U.S. Army BRAC, U.S. EPA, California DTSC, and California Regional Water Quality Control Boards. Compliance Standards: All analyses must be conducted by Department of Defense (DoD) Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (ELAP)-accredited laboratories per DoD Quality Systems Manual (QSM) Table B-15 using DoD Module 3 data validation with Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS) upload and follow safety compliance per U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Manual (EM) 385-1-1 via an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP). Technical & Key Personnel Qualifications: The Contractor must present an overview of qualified in-house staff or primary teaming partners (e.g., Professional Geologists/Hydrogeologists registered in California, Environmental Engineers with water treatment optimization expertise, Quality Assurance Chemists, and USACE EM 385-1-1 Certified Safety Professionals) and show the ability to identified commercial analytical laboratories possessing active DoD ELAP accreditation for PFAS analysis by LC/MS/MS compliant with DoD QSM criteria. 2. Field Characterization and Waste Management Subsurface Drilling: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must advance continuous soil borings advanced to groundwater (~100 feet below ground surface [bgs]) with discrete depth-interval profiling, conduct the installation of multi-cased wells per the Drilling, American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D5092 construction, and conduct multi-aquifer development including shallow water table (~100 ft bgs), intermediate Upper 180-Foot Aquifer (~225 ft bgs), and deep Seaside Groundwater Basin (up to 500 ft bgs). Groundwater Monitoring: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must conduct baseline, seasonal, and base wide sampling rounds for plume delineation. The Contractor will be expected to have an advanced understanding of the areas subsurface hydrology given the Salinas-Valley Aquitard and its various discontinuities as influenced by local potable water and agricultural pumping variations and inform the Government on modifications to the existing MODFLOW model. The Contractor will be expected to operate and maintain existing multi-well port systems in monitoring wells. Strict PFAS Sampling Cross-Contamination Mitigation: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must adhere to strict avoidance of PFAS-containing field equipment, bailers, tubing, pumps, personal protective equipment (PPE), decontamination reagents, sunscreens, and vehicle materials and of documented PFAS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and field blank / equipment rinsate validation programs. Investigation-Derived Waste (IDW) Protocols: The Contractor must be proficient at handling, containment, characterization, transportation, and disposal/destruction of PFAS-impacted drill cuttings, purge water, development water, and decontamination fluids in strict accordance with DoD and State of California regulations. 3. Specialized Comparative Studies HydraSleeve vs. Low-Flow: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must demonstrate competency in the described field study assessing data quality, bias, and operational efficacy for PFAS passive sampling versus conventional purge techniques. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to evaluate data comparability, turbidity impacts, sampling precision/accuracy, and relative bias for both short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and past experience designing, executing, and reporting side-by-side comparative studies between passive sampling devices (specifically HydraSleeve) and conventional low-flow (minimal drawdown) purging/sampling techniques. Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) Plant Efficacy: The Contractor must evaluate influent, mid-bed, and effluent monitoring campaigns across multiple Groundwater Treatment System (GWTS) facilities for short- and long-chain PFAS removal kinetics and plant optimization comingled with co-contaminants. description: ISBEE Set-Aside � Advanced Practice Provider Physician Assistant/Nurse Practitioner Services Solicitation No. 75H70627Q00018 This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with the HHS-adopted FAR Part 12, as supplemented by the attached solicitation documents. This announcement and its attachments constitute the solicitation. Quotations are requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation No. 75H70627Q00018 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), non-personal Advanced Practice Provider (APP) Physician Assistant (PA) and/or Nurse Practitioner (NP) healthcare services at Rosebud IHS Hospital, Rosebud, South Dakota. The Great Plains Area Indian Health Service (IHS) seeks a Contractor to provide qualified APP personnel sufficient to support two (2) full-time equivalent PA and/or NP positions providing outpatient primary care services at the Rosebud IHS Hospital Outpatient Department Clinic. Services include adult and pediatric primary care, chronic disease management, preventive and wellness services, acute outpatient care, authorized minor procedures, clinical documentation, referrals, care coordination, and quality-improvement activities. The Contractor shall furnish qualified licensed personnel, management, supervision, credentialing and privileging support, licensure and certification maintenance, professional liability insurance, staffing continuity, replacement personnel, and other Contractor-furnished resources necessary to perform the Performance Work Statement (PWS). This acquisition is set aside exclusively for Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs). The assigned NAICS code is 561320, Temporary Help Services, with a small business size standard of $34.0 million in average annual receipts. Quoters shall satisfy the applicable ISBEE eligibility and representation requirements and submit the completed IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation form with their quotations. The anticipated award is a Firm-Fixed-Price, non-personal healthcare services purchase order using a Month-of-Service (MOS) pricing structure. One (1) MOS represents complete monthly performance of the required APP services, including qualified staffing equivalent to two (2) full-time PAs or NPs, scheduled outpatient clinic services, clinical documentation, care coordination, required training, and all other PWS requirements. The anticipated period of performance consists of a three (3)-month base period and three (3) option periods of three (3) months each, for a maximum potential period of performance of twelve (12) months. The anticipated base period is February 1, 2027, through April 30, 2027. Option-period dates will be specified in the resulting purchase order. Services will be performed at the Rosebud IHS Hospital Outpatient Department Clinic, 800 Hospital Drive, Rosebud, South Dakota 57570. Standard outpatient clinic hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding federal holidays, subject to the scheduling requirements identified in the PWS. Section F of the attached solicitation identifies the Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs), service descriptions, quantities, units of measure, and performance periods. Quoters shall complete the price schedule with firm-fixed monthly MOS pricing for the base period and each option period. The Total Evaluated Price will include the base period and all three option periods. Award will be made to the responsible quoter whose quotation conforms to the solicitation requirements and represents the best value to the Government. Evaluation factors are Technical Capability and Management Approach, Past Performance, and Price. When combined, the non-price factors are significantly more important than Price. The Government intends to make a selection from initial quotations but reserves the right to request clarification, additional information, or revised quotations when determined appropriate. Questions must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) Central Standard Time (CST) on November 20, 2026. Quotations must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) CST on November 30, 2026. Submit questions and quotations electronically to David.Jones@ihs.gov, referencing RFQ No. 75H70627Q00018 � Rosebud APP Services in the email subject line. Quoters must have a valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), current System for Award Management (SAM) registration, and satisfy all applicable eligibility, responsibility, and exclusion requirements before award. Applicable solicitation provisions and contract clauses are identified in the attached Provisions and Clauses schedule. Prospective quoters are responsible for reviewing the complete solicitation package, including the Combined Synopsis/Solicitation, PWS and addendum, price schedule, quotation instructions, evaluation criteria, applicable FAR/HHSAR provisions and clauses, IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation form, and any amendments before submitting a quotation.

description: This Sources Sought Notice is for Market Research ONLY to determine the availability, capability and interest of small business firms for a potential small business category type set-aside. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME as this is solely for Market Research. Please do not request such documentation. Requests for any of this information will go unanswered. If the conditions at Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO)19.104-1(a) are met the contracting officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. Accordingly, interested contractors who have the skill, capabilities, and workload capacity to complete the described project (either through self-performance and/or the managing of subcontractors) are invited to provide their capability statements to the point of contact listed below. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential acquisition. The purpose of this notice is to obtain a snapshot of current market capabilities and gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following socioeconomic categories: Certified HUB Zone; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) and 8(a) small business concerns to perform database updates to increase the capabilities, usability, and stability of currently existing applications. Other than small business are encouraged to express interest and submit capability statements as well. Contractors� capabilities will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining an appropriate acquisition strategy to include whether this prospective action is appropriate to be set-aside for the small business community or should proceed as an unrestricted full and open acquisition. Other than small businesses are encouraged to respond to this NOTICE to provide a greater context of current market capabilities. However, per the Federal Acquisition Regulations, preference will be given to the small business categories as listed above. In determining the acquisition strategy, the Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Price order with a Period of Performance of five (5) years from date of award. An estimated solicitation date has not yet been determined. The NAICS Code is 562910, Environmental Remediation Services. The Size Standard in Number of Employees: 1,000 Employees. Product Service Code is B510. GENERAL SCOPE: Regulatory & Data Governance Regulatory Framework: This Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) site is governed by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in which the work must strictly adhere to the developed Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Remedial Investigation (RI) Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) which utilizes the Uniform Federal Policy for Quality Assurance Project Plans (UFP-QAPP). The Contractor must transmit all documents and data via Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS). All actions are dictated by the Federal Facilities Agreement (FFA) with the regulatory community. The Contractor will anticipate significant comments on products generated for this effort and must present technically competent PFAS subject matter experts to address and resolve comments suitable for public consumption per EPA Risk Communication guidelines. The Contractor must demonstrate past experience executing CERCLA work under an active FFA alongside USACE, U.S. Army BRAC, U.S. EPA, California DTSC, and California Regional Water Quality Control Boards. Compliance Standards: All analyses must be conducted by Department of Defense (DoD) Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (ELAP)-accredited laboratories per DoD Quality Systems Manual (QSM) Table B-15 using DoD Module 3 data validation with Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS) upload and follow safety compliance per U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Manual (EM) 385-1-1 via an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP). Technical & Key Personnel Qualifications: The Contractor must present an overview of qualified in-house staff or primary teaming partners (e.g., Professional Geologists/Hydrogeologists registered in California, Environmental Engineers with water treatment optimization expertise, Quality Assurance Chemists, and USACE EM 385-1-1 Certified Safety Professionals) and show the ability to identified commercial analytical laboratories possessing active DoD ELAP accreditation for PFAS analysis by LC/MS/MS compliant with DoD QSM criteria. 2. Field Characterization and Waste Management Subsurface Drilling: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must advance continuous soil borings advanced to groundwater (~100 feet below ground surface [bgs]) with discrete depth-interval profiling, conduct the installation of multi-cased wells per the Drilling, American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D5092 construction, and conduct multi-aquifer development including shallow water table (~100 ft bgs), intermediate Upper 180-Foot Aquifer (~225 ft bgs), and deep Seaside Groundwater Basin (up to 500 ft bgs). Groundwater Monitoring: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must conduct baseline, seasonal, and base wide sampling rounds for plume delineation. The Contractor will be expected to have an advanced understanding of the areas subsurface hydrology given the Salinas-Valley Aquitard and its various discontinuities as influenced by local potable water and agricultural pumping variations and inform the Government on modifications to the existing MODFLOW model. The Contractor will be expected to operate and maintain existing multi-well port systems in monitoring wells. Strict PFAS Sampling Cross-Contamination Mitigation: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must adhere to strict avoidance of PFAS-containing field equipment, bailers, tubing, pumps, personal protective equipment (PPE), decontamination reagents, sunscreens, and vehicle materials and of documented PFAS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and field blank / equipment rinsate validation programs. Investigation-Derived Waste (IDW) Protocols: The Contractor must be proficient at handling, containment, characterization, transportation, and disposal/destruction of PFAS-impacted drill cuttings, purge water, development water, and decontamination fluids in strict accordance with DoD and State of California regulations. 3. Specialized Comparative Studies HydraSleeve vs. Low-Flow: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must demonstrate competency in the described field study assessing data quality, bias, and operational efficacy for PFAS passive sampling versus conventional purge techniques. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to evaluate data comparability, turbidity impacts, sampling precision/accuracy, and relative bias for both short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and past experience designing, executing, and reporting side-by-side comparative studies between passive sampling devices (specifically HydraSleeve) and conventional low-flow (minimal drawdown) purging/sampling techniques. Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) Plant Efficacy: The Contractor must evaluate influent, mid-bed, and effluent monitoring campaigns across multiple Groundwater Treatment System (GWTS) facilities for short- and long-chain PFAS removal kinetics and plant optimization comingled with co-contaminants. The OCLC electronic titles are as follows: WorldShare Management System SubscriptionEZproxy HostedOCLC Meridian. title: NONSKID FOR NAVAL SHIPS/VESSELS
description: The award resulting from this RFP will be an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) supply contract with prepriced ELINS for Nonskid Deck Covering Removal/Replacement onboard U.S. Navy Ships. Nonskid replacement shall be accomplished meeting the following Society for Protective Coatings (SSPC) surface preparation standards: SSPC-SP10/National Association of Corrosion Engineers International (NACE) 2 Near-White Blast Cleaning SSPC-SP 11, Power Tool Cleaning to Bare Metal SSPC-SP12 WJ-3/NACE 5, Surface Preparation and Cleaning of Steel and other Hard Materials by High and Ultra High Pressure Water Jetting Prior to Recoating. Nonskid application will be either MIL-PRF-24667 Type I or Type V roll-on nonskid, Type IV spray on nonskid, or Type XI peel and stick sections.

description: ***THIS NOTICE IS FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY*** The Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) Contract Services Directorate (CSD) seeks sources that can develop complete data dictionaries for the Program Budget Accounting System (PBAS) and Headquarters Accounting and Reporting System (HQARS). title: Forest Service Hand Thinning, MATOC North Rockies/Great Basin
description: Requirement includes a wide variety of non-merchantable vegetation management activities for the purpose of fuels reduction, prescribed burn unit preparation, stand improvement, or unit rehabilitation. Activities could include, but are not limited to, tree thinning, slashing, girdling, pruning, weed and release, release of browse species, slash treatment, hand piling, fuel break construction, Fireline construction, residual tree protection, duff mound removal, unit preparation work, rehabilitation, chipping and related services. Unit boundary/special protection area designation and/or traversing for or within these units may also be included in the activity.

title: 30 RS Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST)
description: This requirement is for procurement of services including providing personnel, services, and management support for the Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST) software. The service will provide timely remote and periodic on-site support to the 30RS for MPST. The service includes maintaining compatibility with upgrades to the RQ-170 Mission Planning System (MPS) software, hardware, and databases by utilizing improved and/or expanded intelligence products. It will also ensure the software accurately represents new and/or improved aircraft capabilities, correct errors and address limitations encountered during operational use. Provide software and database maintenance and support functions to the 30 RS for the Mission Planning Support Tools (MPST) and Advanced Framework for Simulation, Integration and Modeling (AFSIM). The contractor shall provide software programming support for MPST computer program and its integration with AFSIM. All individuals performing on-site on this PWS must have a current adjudicated background investigation and be eligible for access to Top Secret, SCI, SAP information and associated ACCMs. Contractor personnel shall be conversant in the computer programming skills to fully support MPST, the version of AFSIM used by the RQ-170 simulator, be familiar with RQ-170 aircraft survivability, capabilities, Blue/Gray/Red ground and airborne threat systems, and Suppressor modeling capabilities/architecture/function/programming. Suppressor model may contain Foreign Government Information. The contractor shall provide support in training in the use of the version of AFSIM currently being used by the RQ-170. Actual work performance location is the contractor facility with periodic on-site visits to Creech AFB, NV and other classified locations as determined by the government.

title: Pine Bluff Arsenal Testing, Lab and Engineering Services
description: The services provided include surface water, sediment, and fish tissue sampling in streams and large river systems, as well as ambient sediment toxicity testing to determine the effectiveness of corrective measures. Acute and chronic whole effluent toxicity testing is conducted for four NPDES permitted outfalls, with the capability to perform Toxicity Identification Evaluation and Toxicity Reduction Evaluation if needed. Additionally, statistical analysis is compiled and conducted for three RCRA Detection monitoring groundwater assessment reports (covering three regulated units) and twelve RCRA Corrective Action Closure sites annually. Maintenance and updating of the PBA-specific Geographic Information System database is also included. The services encompass preparing industrial stormwater permit renewals, Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans, and stormwater sampling for three outfalls, as well as preparation of Construction SWPPPs and permits. Compliance assistance is provided for SPCC Plan development and review, RCRA Permit development and review, and CAA permit review, renewal, and reporting. The services also support a change of the State of Arkansas Water Quality Standards, Rule 2, for mercury at an NPDES outfall, and assist with contaminant transport investigations in Phillips Creek and the Arkansas River. *Amendment 0001 posted 12 November 2026 *Amendment 0002 posted 19 November 2026

title: DA01--Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology (VISTA) Blood Establishment Computer Software (VBECS) Operations and Maintenance Support II
description: VA is seeking sources that are able to provide full lifecycle sustainment and operational support, and any associated bug/fix development, and regulatory compliance services for the VA s existing Veterans Health Administration s VBECS, an FDA regulated Class II Medical Device Software product. The Contractor will be required to plan, manage, develop bug/fixes, test, deploy, maintain, document, and continuously monitor the VBECS system throughout the DevOps lifecycle. The Contractor will be required to maintain all system related documentation, ensuring accuracy, traceability, and compliance with FDA Quality System Regulations (21 CFR 820), ISO 13485:2016, and VA cybersecurity and privacy requirements. The Contractor will be required to support all activities required to maintain the VBECS s existing Authority to Operate, including preparation, validation, and submission of documentation within the SNOW Continuous Authorization and Monitoring environment, and continuous support for audits, assessments, and security reviews.

title: 30 RS Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST)
description: This requirement is for procurement of services including providing personnel, services, and management support for the Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST) software. The service will provide timely remote and periodic on-site support to the 30RS for MPST. The service includes maintaining compatibility with upgrades to the RQ-170 Mission Planning System (MPS) software, hardware, and databases by utilizing improved and/or expanded intelligence products. It will also ensure the software accurately represents new and/or improved aircraft capabilities, correct errors and address limitations encountered during operational use. Provide software and database maintenance and support functions to the 30 RS for the Mission Planning Support Tools (MPST) and Advanced Framework for Simulation, Integration and Modeling (AFSIM). The contractor shall provide software programming support for MPST computer program and its integration with AFSIM. All individuals performing on-site on this PWS must have a current adjudicated background investigation and be eligible for access to Top Secret, SCI, SAP information and associated ACCMs. Contractor personnel shall be conversant in the computer programming skills to fully support MPST, the version of AFSIM used by the RQ-170 simulator, be familiar with RQ-170 aircraft survivability, capabilities, Blue/Gray/Red ground and airborne threat systems, and Suppressor modeling capabilities/architecture/function/programming. Suppressor model may contain Foreign Government Information. The contractor shall provide support in training in the use of the version of AFSIM currently being used by the RQ-170. Actual work performance location is the contractor facility with periodic on-site visits to Creech AFB, NV and other classified locations as determined by the government.

title: S207--BHVAHCS Building 65 Bat Mitigation Sources Sought
description: The Black Hills VA Healthcare System requires bat mitigation and exclusion services in accordance with the draft Statement of Work (SOW) below. This is a sources sought looking for vendors to perform the services per the SOW for market research purposes. No awards of a contract will be made from this announcement. If you are a vendor that can complete the work described in the SOW with competitive pricing, please send your contact and organization information with a descriptive proof of capability to: Jeffrey.Brown8@va.gov on or before November 30th, 2026. Only emailed responses will be considered. Additionally, please provide answers as appropriate to the following questions in the table below with your response to this sources sought. Failure to respond to the following questions may affect the acquisition strategy. Question # Questions Vendor Responses 1. Identify your organization's socio-economic category. � 2. State whether any of the requested services may be ordered against a government contract awarded to your organization (e.g Federal Supply Schedule (FSS), General Services Administration (GSA), etc.). � 3. State if subcontracting is contemplated for this requirement, what percentage of the work will be subcontracted and for what tasks. � � *If applicable, VAAR 852.219-75 VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction, will apply to the potential solicitation if set-aside for Veteran Owned Small-Businesses or Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small-Businesses.* *If applicable, FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting, will apply to the potential solicitation if set-aside for Small-Businesses.* Draft Statement of Work (SOW) Building 65 Bat Mitigation Black Hills VA Health Care System at Fort Meade, South Dakota General Intention: Contractor shall provide all supervision, tools, labor, materials, hardware, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to complete a turnkey finished project for the following services: Professional Bat abatement in attic of Building 65. Remove bat colonies, conduct bat proofing/exclusion, remove bat guano and insulation (sterilize as needed), sanitize the area, and reinstall insulation. Building 65 is a 2-story building with the attic above. General Requirements: Contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, and incidentals necessary to accomplish work elements and requirements outlined in this Statement of Work (SOW). Where equipment, temporary installations, ingress/egress restrictions or any other consideration is necessary, signage in such areas shall be provided by Contractor. The Contractor shall confine all staging activities within the anticipated construction area. Contractor shall coordinate proposed staging areas with the facility representative for approval. The Contractor shall field verify all existing conditions, dimensions, and quantities prior to any work activities. Time and date to be coordinated with facility representative. Any work that is not addressed by the contract shall immediately be brought to the attention of the Contracting Officer. No out-of-scope or additional work shall be executed prior to modification of the contract by the Contracting Officer. Contractor shall remove all rubbish from the Fort Meade property and dispose off site following VA Specification 01 74 19 Construction Waste Management. Contractor shall record all quantities of materials removed from the Fort Meade property and turn into the facility representative monthly reports even if a null report. Contractor to perform all work during normal work hours, Monday through Friday 7:00 am to 4:30 pm Mountain Time except as coordinated with the facility representative for any activities that may need to occur outside of normal working hours at no additional cost to the Government. The requirements of this SOW supplement other related VA standards for construction, space and facility planning criteria, design guides, design manuals, specifications, and details, which remain in full force and effect. Specifically, all requirements of VA handbook 0730, NEC 517, NFPA Health Care Facilities Code for Branches, Security and Law Enforcement, Appendix B, (which covers physical security requirements for VA facilities), the VA fire Protection Design Manual (which covers all VA construction), and ICT standards on the TIL remain in effect. Work Elements: Which shall include and are not limited to: All supervision, tools, labor, materials, hardware, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to complete a turnkey finished project. Bat Exclusion: Bats need to be permanently excluded from roosting in the VA building 65 using non-lethal exclusion methods following Bat Conservation International (BCI), South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks recommendations, and comply with section 7 of the Endangered Species Act. The technique includes using one-way exit devices (industry preferred exclusion tubes VA approved), sealing points of entry, interior and exterior of the building, and preventing access to the building interior. Exclusion activities will be conducted when bats are not present if feasible; this timing will also ensure that activities occur before the Maternity and Roost season. Bat removal shall occur between February 1st, 2027 and April 15th, 2027. Exclusion may not be done when pups are too young to fly (June-August). Change to these timelines may be proposed and accepted after discussion and approval by the designated facility representative(s) and contracting officer. One-way exit devices through which bats can leave but cannot return are made from tube-type excluders which are placed at all active entry points. Exclusion tubes should have a diameter of two inches, a length of 10 inches with a smooth surface and should project no more than one-quarter inch into the opening. Once the tube has been secured over the hole, a piece of lightweight, clear plastic can be taped around the tubes outside end to further reduce the likelihood of bats reentering, though this may not be necessary. Multiple exclusion tubes may be required. Lightweight, flexible plastic netting with one-sixth-inch mesh or smaller can be used to form a one-way valve over openings on smooth surfaces of exterior walls or attic louvers. The one-way exit devices will remain in place for at least five to seven days. The devices will be removed after all bats have been confirmed to be excluded. Night observation and other means, may be needed when determining if bats are still entering or leaving the building. It must be confirmed by visual inspection or other that bats are no longer present. Sealing Exclusion Points Exclusion points will be sealed with OSI silicone sealant, caulk backing rod, hardware cloth or heavy-duty polypropylene mesh, flashing out required areas around roofline with proper metal for optimal coverage. If one-way exit devices have been used, sealing will be conducted after the five-to-seven days that the devices have been in place. Bats can enter buildings or living spaces through openings as small as 3/8 diameter. Focus points include but not limited to trim, soffits, chimneys, and dormers. All metal on the front roofs will be properly sealed and securely screwed down where required to prevent Bat re-entering the building. Appropriate screws designed for metal, equipped with washers to prevent leaks will be used, and sealed to prevent future water damage. Preventing Building Interior Access The building s interior will be inspected for small openings through which bats could enter. Bats can enter buildings or living spaces through openings as small as 3/8 diameter. All openings connecting potential roosting areas to living quarters need to be sealed. Methods not to be used for bat exclusion: Simply waiting for bats to fly out at night and then permanently sealing the entrances without the use of one-way exit devices. title: Remedial Investigation (RI) and Optional Feasibility Study (FS) for Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS)
description: This Sources Sought Notice is for Market Research ONLY to determine the availability, capability and interest of small business firms for a potential small business category type set-aside. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME as this is solely for Market Research. Please do not request such documentation. Requests for any of this information will go unanswered. If the conditions at Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO)19.104-1(a) are met the contracting officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. Accordingly, interested contractors who have the skill, capabilities, and workload capacity to complete the described project (either through self-performance and/or the managing of subcontractors) are invited to provide their capability statements to the point of contact listed below. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential acquisition. The purpose of this notice is to obtain a snapshot of current market capabilities and gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following socioeconomic categories: Certified HUB Zone; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) and 8(a) small business concerns to perform database updates to increase the capabilities, usability, and stability of currently existing applications. Other than small business are encouraged to express interest and submit capability statements as well. Contractors� capabilities will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining an appropriate acquisition strategy to include whether this prospective action is appropriate to be set-aside for the small business community or should proceed as an unrestricted full and open acquisition. Other than small businesses are encouraged to respond to this NOTICE to provide a greater context of current market capabilities. However, per the Federal Acquisition Regulations, preference will be given to the small business categories as listed above. In determining the acquisition strategy, the Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Price order with a Period of Performance of five (5) years from date of award. An estimated solicitation date has not yet been determined. The NAICS Code is 562910, Environmental Remediation Services. The Size Standard in Number of Employees: 1,000 Employees. Product Service Code is B510. GENERAL SCOPE: Regulatory & Data Governance Regulatory Framework: This Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) site is governed by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in which the work must strictly adhere to the developed Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Remedial Investigation (RI) Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) which utilizes the Uniform Federal Policy for Quality Assurance Project Plans (UFP-QAPP). The Contractor must transmit all documents and data via Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS). All actions are dictated by the Federal Facilities Agreement (FFA) with the regulatory community. The Contractor will anticipate significant comments on products generated for this effort and must present technically competent PFAS subject matter experts to address and resolve comments suitable for public consumption per EPA Risk Communication guidelines. The Contractor must demonstrate past experience executing CERCLA work under an active FFA alongside USACE, U.S. Army BRAC, U.S. EPA, California DTSC, and California Regional Water Quality Control Boards. Compliance Standards: All analyses must be conducted by Department of Defense (DoD) Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (ELAP)-accredited laboratories per DoD Quality Systems Manual (QSM) Table B-15 using DoD Module 3 data validation with Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS) upload and follow safety compliance per U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Manual (EM) 385-1-1 via an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP). Technical & Key Personnel Qualifications: The Contractor must present an overview of qualified in-house staff or primary teaming partners (e.g., Professional Geologists/Hydrogeologists registered in California, Environmental Engineers with water treatment optimization expertise, Quality Assurance Chemists, and USACE EM 385-1-1 Certified Safety Professionals) and show the ability to identified commercial analytical laboratories possessing active DoD ELAP accreditation for PFAS analysis by LC/MS/MS compliant with DoD QSM criteria. 2. Field Characterization and Waste Management Subsurface Drilling: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must advance continuous soil borings advanced to groundwater (~100 feet below ground surface [bgs]) with discrete depth-interval profiling, conduct the installation of multi-cased wells per the Drilling, American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D5092 construction, and conduct multi-aquifer development including shallow water table (~100 ft bgs), intermediate Upper 180-Foot Aquifer (~225 ft bgs), and deep Seaside Groundwater Basin (up to 500 ft bgs). Groundwater Monitoring: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must conduct baseline, seasonal, and base wide sampling rounds for plume delineation. The Contractor will be expected to have an advanced understanding of the areas subsurface hydrology given the Salinas-Valley Aquitard and its various discontinuities as influenced by local potable water and agricultural pumping variations and inform the Government on modifications to the existing MODFLOW model. The Contractor will be expected to operate and maintain existing multi-well port systems in monitoring wells. Strict PFAS Sampling Cross-Contamination Mitigation: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must adhere to strict avoidance of PFAS-containing field equipment, bailers, tubing, pumps, personal protective equipment (PPE), decontamination reagents, sunscreens, and vehicle materials and of documented PFAS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and field blank / equipment rinsate validation programs. Investigation-Derived Waste (IDW) Protocols: The Contractor must be proficient at handling, containment, characterization, transportation, and disposal/destruction of PFAS-impacted drill cuttings, purge water, development water, and decontamination fluids in strict accordance with DoD and State of California regulations. 3. Specialized Comparative Studies HydraSleeve vs. Low-Flow: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must demonstrate competency in the described field study assessing data quality, bias, and operational efficacy for PFAS passive sampling versus conventional purge techniques. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to evaluate data comparability, turbidity impacts, sampling precision/accuracy, and relative bias for both short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and past experience designing, executing, and reporting side-by-side comparative studies between passive sampling devices (specifically HydraSleeve) and conventional low-flow (minimal drawdown) purging/sampling techniques. Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) Plant Efficacy: The Contractor must evaluate influent, mid-bed, and effluent monitoring campaigns across multiple Groundwater Treatment System (GWTS) facilities for short- and long-chain PFAS removal kinetics and plant optimization comingled with co-contaminants. description: THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION ABOUT PRICING, DELIVERY, THE MARKET, AND CAPABILITIES IS HIGHLY ENCOURAGED AND ALLOWED UNDER THIS RFI FOR PLANNING PURPOSES IN ACCORDANCE WITH (IAW) FAR 15.201(e). All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly. IAW FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. SOURCES SOUGHT/RFI DESCRIPTION This is NOT a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice / RFI only. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice / RFI is to gain information about potential qualified sources and their size classification relative to NAICS code is 339112 -Medical surgical instruments equipment and supplies, with an SBA small business size standard of 1,000 employees. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. After review of the responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI, further RFIs and/or a solicitation or other announcements may be published. The purpose of this procurement is to acquire SUREPOWER rechargeable lithium-ion battery packs and R Series WiFi Cards with Clock Sync, FIPS, for defibrillators used throughout the facility by Nursing staff. The batteries shall power the defibrillators used on crash carts. The R Series WiFi Cards shall provide network connectivity, with clock synchronization performed automatically through DXS after scheduled readiness tests. The anticipated requirement includes battery packs with 5.8 Ah capacity, high-density lithium-ion chemistry, a RunTime Indicator, automatic calibration readiness, and the ability to store use and maintenance history. The WiFi Cards shall meet the physical, wireless, security, environmental, certification, and operating-system requirements identified in the Statement of Work below. The contractor shall comply with the complete VA cybersecurity and privacy requirements included in the Statement of Work, including the requirements applicable to medical devices, specialized systems, wireless connectivity, FIPS-validated cryptography, patching, product integrity, incident reporting, and VA information-system access. STATEMENT OF WORK Description of Equipment Requested: SUREPOWER RECHARGEABLE LITHIUM-ION BATTERY PACK and R Series WiFi Card with Clock Sync, FIPS for defibrillators How Equipment Works: Batteries power the defibrillators to enable them to deliver a controlled electrical shock that depolarizes all heart muscle cells at once, stopping chaotic rhythms like ventricular fibrillation so the heart s natural pacemaker can restart a normal rhythm. This process is performed by devices such as AEDs, which analyze heart rhythms and shock only when needed. The R Series Wi Fi card enables network connectivity, while clock synchronization is performed automatically through DXS after scheduled readiness tests. Who Will Use This Equipment: Nursing staff Where it will be used: Throughout the facility Salient Characteristics: Battery Must have 5.8 Ah Capacity Must have High density lithium-ion chemistry Must have RunTime Indicator Must have Automatic calibration ready Must be able to store history of use and maintenance R Series Wifi Card Must have Standard: IEEE 802.11 a/b/g/n (single stream) Must have Interface: CompactFlash (CF) self contained CF to Wi Fi functionality (no host CPU load) Must have Bands: 2.4 GHz (2.412 2.462 GHz) & 5 GHz (5.180 5.825 GHz) Must have Data rates: Up to 65 Mbps (includes 54/58.5/52/39/26/19.5/13/6/5/5.5/2/1 Mbps) Must have Modulation: OFDM with BPSK, QPSK, 16QAM, 64QAM, CCK Must have Security: WPA/WPA2 PSK, WEP (64/128 bits), TKIP Must have Antenna: Embedded PCB printed, 1.30 dBi @ 2.4 GHz / 1.97 dBi @ 5 GHz Must have TX power: 9 dBm @ 802.11a, 14 dBm @ 802.11b, 11 dBm @ 802.11g, 10 dBm @ 802.11n, 8 dBm @ 802.11an Must have Sensitivity: 70 dBm @ 802.11a, 75 dBm @ 802.11b, 70 dBm @ 802.11g, 69 dBm @ 802.11n, 67 dBm @ 802.11an Must have Dimensions: 60.5 × 41.7 × 6.45 mm Must have Operating temp: 0 55 °C Must have Humidity: 20 % 95 % Must have Certifications: FCC, IC Must have OS support: Windows XP / 7 Additional Equipment Or Replacement Equipment (EE number): Replacement Equipment No EE#s - MVO Justification: Defibrillators are required for crash carts VA CYBERSECURITY AND PRIVACY LANGUAGE FOR INCLUSION IN ACQUISITIONS. title: S207--BHVAHCS Building 65 Bat Mitigation Sources Sought
description: The Black Hills VA Healthcare System requires bat mitigation and exclusion services in accordance with the draft Statement of Work (SOW) below. This is a sources sought looking for vendors to perform the services per the SOW for market research purposes. No awards of a contract will be made from this announcement. If you are a vendor that can complete the work described in the SOW with competitive pricing, please send your contact and organization information with a descriptive proof of capability to: Jeffrey.Brown8@va.gov on or before November 30th, 2026. Only emailed responses will be considered. Additionally, please provide answers as appropriate to the following questions in the table below with your response to this sources sought. Failure to respond to the following questions may affect the acquisition strategy. Question # Questions Vendor Responses 1. Identify your organization's socio-economic category. � 2. State whether any of the requested services may be ordered against a government contract awarded to your organization (e.g Federal Supply Schedule (FSS), General Services Administration (GSA), etc.). � 3. State if subcontracting is contemplated for this requirement, what percentage of the work will be subcontracted and for what tasks. � � *If applicable, VAAR 852.219-75 VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction, will apply to the potential solicitation if set-aside for Veteran Owned Small-Businesses or Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small-Businesses.* *If applicable, FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting, will apply to the potential solicitation if set-aside for Small-Businesses.* Draft Statement of Work (SOW) Building 65 Bat Mitigation Black Hills VA Health Care System at Fort Meade, South Dakota General Intention: Contractor shall provide all supervision, tools, labor, materials, hardware, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to complete a turnkey finished project for the following services: Professional Bat abatement in attic of Building 65. Remove bat colonies, conduct bat proofing/exclusion, remove bat guano and insulation (sterilize as needed), sanitize the area, and reinstall insulation. Building 65 is a 2-story building with the attic above. General Requirements: Contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, and incidentals necessary to accomplish work elements and requirements outlined in this Statement of Work (SOW). Where equipment, temporary installations, ingress/egress restrictions or any other consideration is necessary, signage in such areas shall be provided by Contractor. The Contractor shall confine all staging activities within the anticipated construction area. Contractor shall coordinate proposed staging areas with the facility representative for approval. The Contractor shall field verify all existing conditions, dimensions, and quantities prior to any work activities. Time and date to be coordinated with facility representative. Any work that is not addressed by the contract shall immediately be brought to the attention of the Contracting Officer. No out-of-scope or additional work shall be executed prior to modification of the contract by the Contracting Officer. Contractor shall remove all rubbish from the Fort Meade property and dispose off site following VA Specification 01 74 19 Construction Waste Management. Contractor shall record all quantities of materials removed from the Fort Meade property and turn into the facility representative monthly reports even if a null report. Contractor to perform all work during normal work hours, Monday through Friday 7:00 am to 4:30 pm Mountain Time except as coordinated with the facility representative for any activities that may need to occur outside of normal working hours at no additional cost to the Government. The requirements of this SOW supplement other related VA standards for construction, space and facility planning criteria, design guides, design manuals, specifications, and details, which remain in full force and effect. Specifically, all requirements of VA handbook 0730, NEC 517, NFPA Health Care Facilities Code for Branches, Security and Law Enforcement, Appendix B, (which covers physical security requirements for VA facilities), the VA fire Protection Design Manual (which covers all VA construction), and ICT standards on the TIL remain in effect. Work Elements: Which shall include and are not limited to: All supervision, tools, labor, materials, hardware, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to complete a turnkey finished project. Bat Exclusion: Bats need to be permanently excluded from roosting in the VA building 65 using non-lethal exclusion methods following Bat Conservation International (BCI), South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks recommendations, and comply with section 7 of the Endangered Species Act. The technique includes using one-way exit devices (industry preferred exclusion tubes VA approved), sealing points of entry, interior and exterior of the building, and preventing access to the building interior. Exclusion activities will be conducted when bats are not present if feasible; this timing will also ensure that activities occur before the Maternity and Roost season. Bat removal shall occur between February 1st, 2027 and April 15th, 2027. Exclusion may not be done when pups are too young to fly (June-August). Change to these timelines may be proposed and accepted after discussion and approval by the designated facility representative(s) and contracting officer. One-way exit devices through which bats can leave but cannot return are made from tube-type excluders which are placed at all active entry points. Exclusion tubes should have a diameter of two inches, a length of 10 inches with a smooth surface and should project no more than one-quarter inch into the opening. Once the tube has been secured over the hole, a piece of lightweight, clear plastic can be taped around the tubes outside end to further reduce the likelihood of bats reentering, though this may not be necessary. Multiple exclusion tubes may be required. Lightweight, flexible plastic netting with one-sixth-inch mesh or smaller can be used to form a one-way valve over openings on smooth surfaces of exterior walls or attic louvers. The one-way exit devices will remain in place for at least five to seven days. The devices will be removed after all bats have been confirmed to be excluded. Night observation and other means, may be needed when determining if bats are still entering or leaving the building. It must be confirmed by visual inspection or other that bats are no longer present. Sealing Exclusion Points Exclusion points will be sealed with OSI silicone sealant, caulk backing rod, hardware cloth or heavy-duty polypropylene mesh, flashing out required areas around roofline with proper metal for optimal coverage. If one-way exit devices have been used, sealing will be conducted after the five-to-seven days that the devices have been in place. Bats can enter buildings or living spaces through openings as small as 3/8 diameter. Focus points include but not limited to trim, soffits, chimneys, and dormers. All metal on the front roofs will be properly sealed and securely screwed down where required to prevent Bat re-entering the building. Appropriate screws designed for metal, equipped with washers to prevent leaks will be used, and sealed to prevent future water damage. Preventing Building Interior Access The building s interior will be inspected for small openings through which bats could enter. Bats can enter buildings or living spaces through openings as small as 3/8 diameter. All openings connecting potential roosting areas to living quarters need to be sealed. Methods not to be used for bat exclusion: Simply waiting for bats to fly out at night and then permanently sealing the entrances without the use of one-way exit devices. description: The previous RFI number 36C10B27Q0056 was corrupted in the system. This RFI replaces 36C10B27Q0056 and continues the previous RFI progress. The Contractor will be required to plan, manage, develop bug/fixes, test, deploy, maintain, document, and continuously monitor the VBECS system throughout the DevOps lifecycle. The Contractor will be required to maintain all system related documentation, ensuring accuracy, traceability, and compliance with FDA Quality System Regulations (21 CFR 820), ISO 13485:2016, and VA cybersecurity and privacy requirements. The Contractor will be required to support all activities required to maintain the VBECS s existing Authority to Operate, including preparation, validation, and submission of documentation within the SNOW Continuous Authorization and Monitoring environment, and continuous support for audits, assessments, and security reviews. This amendment is to provide answers to questions asked in response to this RFI and to provide a revised PWS.

title: MACH1_AOI_Military Working Dog Facility_ Vandenberg Space Force_LOE 1 and LOE 2
description: This Area of Interest (AOI) is published under the Modernized Agile Construction Horizons (MACH1) Umbrella Program Notice. All submissions must adhere to the procedures and guidelines outlined in the parent MACH1 framework document unless otherwise tailored herein. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS) is is executing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) project to renovate existing military working dog (MWD) facilities and construct a new addition at Vandenberg Space Force Base (SFB), California. Under this agreement, the selected contractor will execute both the progressive design and physical construction to deliver a fully functional, code-compliant compound (Project Number: XUMU171121C). The current MWD kennel and admin facilities (Buildings 6444 and 6447) at Vandenberg SFB fail quarterly inspections and contain critical safety hazards that endanger military personnel and canine assets. Transitioning to a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) model is critical to eliminate traditional design-bid-build delays, rapidly deliver compliant spaces, and preserve the security mission of the 30th Space Wing. There are (2) two distinct lines of effort (LOEs) for this requirement: LOE 1 - Design & Planning (Design) and LOE 2 - Physical Construction. title: JBSA Lodging Revised Solicitation
description: Purpose of Amendment: The purpose of this amendment is to formally amend the subject solicitation as follows: Extension of Solicitation Due Date: The offer/quote submission deadline is hereby extended from 10 November 2026 to 30 November 2026, at 12:00 PM CDT. Acknowledgment and Acceptance of Amendment: Offerors must acknowledge receipt of this amendment prior to the revised hour and date specified for receipt of offers. Offerors shall acknowledge receipt by completing, signing, and returning the standard form (SF 1449 / SF 30). Returning the signed SF 1449 with the offerors submission constitutes full acceptance and acknowledgment of this amendment. Failure to acknowledge this amendment may result in rejection of the offer._____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________Solicitation Notice: Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Commercial Lodging BPA (FA301627Q0008)Scope of Work The 502d Contracting Squadron (502 CONS CL) at JBSA Lackland, Texas, is soliciting quotes to establish up to six (6) decentralized, firm-fixed-price Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) for commercial off-base lodging accommodations. The selected contractors will provide clean, safe, and secure single and double occupancy lodging rooms within a 15-mile driving radius of JBSA-Lackland or JBSA-Fort Sam Houston to support transient military and civilian personnel. The agreements will cover a 12-month base period with four subsequent one-year option periods. All direct-billed government reservations must be processed as tax-exempt. Key Deadlines and Submission Details: Quote Submission Deadline: All electronic quotes must be fully submitted and received no later than 12:00 PM CST on November 10, 2026.Contractor Questions and Answers Deadline: Technical or administrative questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted using the designated Questions and Answers spreadsheet (Attachment 05) no later than 12:00 PM CST on October 28, 2026.Points of Contact for Submission: Submissions and questions must be sent via email directly to the primary Contract Specialist, SrA Autumn Mauran (autumn.mauran@us.af.mil), the Primary Contracting Officer, Doralo Fuller (doralo.fuller@us.af.mil), and CC Contracting Officer, Thomas Farrell (thomas.farrell.5@us.af.mil).Required Submission Documents: To be eligible for evaluation, contractors must electronically submit: completed and signed SF 1449 capability statement demonstrating active SAM.gov registration and small business status under NAICS code 721110 completed pricing lists (Attachment 03)FEMA fire safety and ADA compliance documentation completed Pre-Award Assessment Checklist (Attachment 04).
