title: ISBEE Solicitation: Emergency Department Registered Nurse Services (Up to 8 RNs) � Standing Rock Service Unit, Fort Yates IHS Hospital, Fort Yates, ND.
description: The Indian Health Service (IHS), Great Plains Area, is soliciting proposals for non-personal Emergency Department Registered Nurse services in support of the Standing Rock Service Unit, Fort Yates Hospital, Fort Yates, North Dakota, under Solicitation No. 75H70627R00002. The requirement is for up to eight (8) qualified Emergency Department Registered Nurse positions to support continuous 24-hour, 7-day-per-week Emergency Department operations. The anticipated contract type is Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), commercial services, with one four (4)-month Base Period and fourteen (14) four-month Option Periods, for a total potential period of performance of sixty (60) months. This acquisition is set aside 100 percent for eligible Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) in accordance with the Buy Indian Act and applicable HHSAR requirements. The applicable NAICS code is 561320, Temporary Help Services, and the Product Service Code is Q401, Medical�Nursing. The Contractor will be responsible for providing qualified nursing personnel and all associated management, supervision, recruitment, credentialing, scheduling, replacement staffing, administrative support, and other resources necessary to perform the requirements of the Performance Work Statement. The requirement consists of up to eight (8) separately exercisable RN positions. The Base Period provides for up to eight (8) RN position CLINs, with the actual number of Base Period RN position CLINs awarded or funded identified in the resulting contract. During each Option Period, the Government may independently exercise from one (1) up to eight (8) RN position CLINs based on operational requirements and availability of funds. The Government is not obligated to award, fund, or exercise all eight RN positions, any particular RN position, or any Option Period. Pricing will be based on a common Firm-Fixed-Price RN Month of Service (RN/MOS) unit price for each performance period. The common RN/MOS unit price will apply uniformly to all RN positions within that performance period. The Total Evaluated Price will be based on the maximum potential requirement for the Base Period and all fourteen Option Periods; evaluation of all RN position CLINs and option prices does not obligate the Government to award, fund, or exercise all positions or options. Important Dates: Questions regarding the solicitation are due no later than November 13, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time. Proposals are due no later than November 30, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time. Award will be made using a Best Value Tradeoff process. Evaluation factors are Past Performance, Technical Approach, Management Approach, and Price. Past Performance, Technical Approach, and Management Approach, when combined, are more important than Price. Technical Approach and Management Approach will be evaluated using adjectival ratings of Outstanding, Good, Acceptable, Marginal, or Unacceptable. The Government may select a higher-priced proposal when the evaluated benefits of the non-price factors justify the associated price premium. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the complete solicitation package, including the Performance Work Statement, Price Schedule/Bid Sheet, applicable FAR/HHSAR provisions and clauses, Buy Indian Act/ISBEE representations, wage determination, and any amendments, prior to submitting an offer.

title: Department of War Pharmacy Uniform Formulary Blanket Purchase Agreement/Uniform Formulary Additional Discount Program
description: The Department of War (DoW) is required by law (10 U.S.C. � 1074g) to establish an effective, efficient, integrated pharmacy benefits program for the Military Health System (MHS) which includes the purchase pharmaceutical agents. The law and implementing regulation (32 CFR Section 199.21) describe the process by which the DoW Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee will consider the relative clinical effectiveness and relative cost effectiveness of pharmaceutical agents in a therapeutic class in recommending the selection of agents for the DoW Uniform Formulary (UF) and, for cost sharing purposes, the classification of a pharmaceutical agent as generic, formulary, Basic Core Formulary (BCF), Extended Core Formulary (ECF), or non-formulary (NF). Prior to the scheduled P&T Committee meeting, a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for pharmaceutical agents within Drug Classes identified for placement on the UF has been issued to obtain quotes from industry. The Defense Health Agency may award Uniform Formulary Blanket Purchase Agreements (UF BPA) and the Uniform Formulary Additional Discount Program Agreements (UF ADP) based on the UF decision. This process is described in the attached RFQ. P&T COMMITTEE MEETING: The following February 2027 newly approved drugs will be reviewed: Atebrioz � Skeletal Muscle Relaxants and Combinations � Subclass: NA Emcitate � Thyroid and Antithyroid Agents � Subclass: NA Hibsago � Hepatitis B Agents � Subclass: NA Juvmo � Parkinsons Agents � Subclass: NA Zegfrovy � Lung Cancer � Subclass: EGFR+ NSCLC The RFQ, including UF BPA and UF ADP appendices, are attached herein. title: S222--Sources Sought - Hazardous Waste Removal/Disposal Northeast Ohio VA Healthcare System - Cleveland, OH
description: Hazardous Waste Pickup, Transportation, and Disposal Services, Cleveland VA Medical Center and Supported CBOCs CORRECTION NOTICE: This notice re-issues Sources Sought 36C25026Q0957, which closed on September 14, 2026. Question #4 of that notice referred to "Scrap Metal Recycling services" in error. The requirement is for hazardous waste services. Questions #4 through #7 below replace the original Question #4. Firms that responded to the original notice may revise and resubmit their responses, answering Questions #4 through #7, but are not required to. Firms that did not respond are encouraged to respond now. The Network Contracting Office (NCO 10) is seeking vendors to perform Hazardous Waste Pickup, Transportation, and Disposal Services at the Cleveland VA Medical Center and its supported Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs). This is a Sources Sought to identify capable sources and request industry feedback ONLY. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. Interested parties are asked to answer the questions below AND submit a capability statement that clearly and convincingly demonstrates their ability to fulfill the requirement. The capability statement and answers to the questions below must be submitted electronically by email to Joshua.Kovar@VA.gov no later than 1:30 PM EST on November 30, 2026. As part of market research, this Sources Sought is intended to determine whether an adequate number of qualified, interested contractors exists that are capable of providing the requirement. Industry feedback is requested to ensure the VA has not created a "de facto sole source" requirement. The Government may use the responses for information and planning purposes. DRAFT SCOPE: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of providing hazardous waste services at the Cleveland VA Medical Center and a number of CBOCs throughout Northeast, Central, and Northwest Ohio. The contractor will provide on-site support, packaging, transportation, and treatment and disposal of hazardous waste. The estimated hazardous waste volume is approximately 68,000 to 75,000 pounds per year. This estimate is provided solely for informational and market research purposes. The forthcoming solicitation will include a refined workload estimate based on updated facility data. The Government is proposing an Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with a five-year ordering period. The Government anticipates placing a task order each year to cover that year's requirements. QUESTIONS FOR INDUSTRY Question #1. Are you interested in providing a quote for this requirement? (Yes / No) Question #2. Please provide your company name, address, UEI, and a point of contact. State your business size under the NAICS code below and any SBA certifications (for example, SDVOSB, VOSB, WOSB, EDWOSB, HUBZone, 8(a), small business). Veteran-owned firms should state their SBA VetCert status. Question #3. What is your current scope of operations and locations of service? Where do you currently work, and what is your maximum service area? Please state your ability to perform in Cleveland and in the CBOC locations across Northeast, Central, and Northwest Ohio. Question #4: Collection and packaging. Does your firm self-perform hazardous waste collection and on-site packaging with its own employees? (Yes / No) If no, what type of subcontractor would you use? Question #5: Transportation. Does your firm self-perform hazardous waste transportation with its own vehicles and drivers? (Yes / No) If no, what type of subcontractor would you use? Question #6: Treatment and disposal. Does your firm own or operate the permitted facility that treats or disposes of the hazardous waste? (Yes / No) If no, what type of subcontractor or facility would you use? Question #7: Licenses and permits. Does your firm hold, or have access through a subcontractor, the federal and state licenses and permits required to transport and dispose of hazardous waste in Ohio? (Yes / No) Answers to Questions #4 through #7 are for market research only and will help the Government understand industry practices and self-performance capabilities. CAPABILITY STATEMENT Please provide a capability statement that supports this requirement. Include relevant past performance, preferably hazardous waste services at a medical center or similar healthcare facility. NAICS AND PSC The applicable NAICS code is 562211, Hazardous Waste Treatment and Disposal, with a small business size standard of $47.0 million. The Product Service Code is S222, Housekeeping Waste Treatment/Storage. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond. Each respondent must identify its business size in its capability statement and answer the questions above. DISCLAIMER This Sources Sought is only for the purpose of identifying potential sources as part of market research. No Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or Invitation for Bid (IFB) exists. Responses are not quotes, proposals, or bids on which the VA can issue a contract. This notice is issued for information and planning purposes only. The Government does not intend to award a contract based only on responses to this Sources Sought. Responses will not be returned. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding, and the VA will not pay for information received. Do not submit pricing information.

title: Yuma Proving Ground Job Order Contract (JOC)
description: SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS Job Order Contract for Yuma Proving Ground This is a Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS) ONLY. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the U.S. Government is not seeking quotes, bids or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this sources sought synopsis. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, IFB, or RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Government wide Point of Entry (GPE). It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor the GPE for additional information pertaining to this requirement. The GPE is located at https://sam.gov. The United States (U.S.) Government desires to procure a Job Order Contract (JOC) at Yuma Proving Ground, on a small business set-aside basis, provided 2 or more qualified small businesses respond to this sources sought synopsis with information sufficient to support a set-aside. Be advised that the U.S. Government will not be able to set aside this requirement if two (2) or more small businesses do not respond with information to support the set-aside. We encourage all small businesses, in all socioeconomic categories (including, 8(a) Business Development Program, Small Disadvantage Business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned Small Business concerns), to identify their capabilities in meeting the requirement at a fair market price. BACKGROUND: A continuing need is anticipated for a job order contract at Yuma Proving Ground. Attached you will find the draft Statement of Work (SOW). The Government contract for these services was previously performed under contract W91151-21-D-0012. The Period of Performance ended 1 August 2026. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and construction services as defined in this SOW. The NAICS code for the requirement is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction with a corresponding size standard of $45 million. If your company believes a different NAICS code would better fit this requirement, please tell us your suggested NAICS and why it would better fit this requirement. The Contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, personnel, equipment, materials, and supplies, with the exception of Government Furnished Property (GFP), to perform activities under this Job Order Contract. PURPOSE OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT: To request information on capabilities of potential offerors to provide the services described herein. Electronic submissions only: Responses are due no later than 13:00pm CDT on 30 November 2026 to facilitate planning and ensure maximum consideration. The email attachments cannot exceed 9 megabytes (MB) due to the Government�s email system restrictions. DO NOT SEND ZIPPED files as the Government�s network will remove all zipped files. Interested businesses should provide a brief capability statement package (limited to no more than 30 pages, single spaced, and 12 font size minimum) demonstrating specific capability in reference to this requirement. The Government prefers that your firm submits its response in Microsoft Word, Adobe Acrobat, or a combination of the two and the document(s) must be searchable. Include: Whether the experience has been as a prime contractor or subcontractor on similar requirements (include the services provided, the number of facilities involved, and any other relevant information you deem applicable). Email the capability package to: Marissa Joyner - Contract Specialist at email: Marissa.joyner.civ@army.mil and Andrew Graham - Contracting Officer at email: Andrew.s.graham6.civ@army.mil The email subject line should include: The Firm�s Name, �Response to the Sources Sought Synopsis for the JOC at Yuma Proving Ground, W5168W-26-R-A022". **Note: the location(s) and corresponding solicitation number that you are responding to must be identified on the subject line. In response to this sources sought, please provide: 1. A company�s profile must include: The name of the firm, point of contact, phone number, email address, number of employees, annual revenue history, CAGE code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). number. Respondents must also indicate small business certification status, for example: Small Business (SB), Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), 8(a), Economically Disadvantaged Woman Owned SB (EDWOSB), WOSB, HUBZone, or Service Disabled Veteran Owned SB (SDVOSB). 2. Respond to: What fundamental tasks you believe need to be performed to successfully accomplish the job order contract? In essence, what primary tasks should be used for determining minimum capability to provide these services? 3. Whether your firm is interested in competing for this requirement as a prime contractor. If you are subcontracting any of the services out, contemplating a Joint Venture, and/or creating a teaming arrangement, please provide the name of these companies and what work they will be performing, if available. Please provide your company�s specific experience in job order contracts and providing comparable services. Ensure the information is in sufficiently detailed regarding previous experience in managing job order contracts (indicate whether the experience has been as a prime contractor or subcontractor) on similar requirements (include the services provided, the number of facilities involved, and any other relevant information you deem applicable). If applicable, please provide the same experience information from any subcontracts, Joint Venture, and/or teaming partners you may propose with. 4. What percentage of work will be performed by the small business prime contractor and all similarly situated entity subcontractors? Note: In accordance with FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (Oct 2022) and Class Deviation 2021-O0008, Revision 1 - Limitations on Subcontracting for Small Business (Feb 2023), for general construction under NAICS 236220, prime contractor and similarly situated subcontractors must perform at least 15% of the cost of the contract, excluding the cost of materials. 5. Type(s)/certifications(s) of proposed subcontractors (for example, SDB, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB). 6. Information on the financial capacity of your business to meet financial obligations (i.e. payroll, payment of subcontractors, etc.). 7. How the Army can best structure these contract requirements to facilitate competition by and among small business concerns. 8. Identify any condition or action that may have the effect of unnecessarily restricting competition with respect to this acquisition. Please contact the MICC Advocate for Competition, Scott Kukes at email: scott.d.kukes.civ@army.mil or 210-466-3015, if you believe that this action is unreasonably restricting competition. Include the subject of the acquisition, this announcement, and the MICC POC information from the notice on https://sam.gov. Provide the specific aspects that unreasonably restrict competition and the rationale for such conclusion.

title: H199--FY27 Cathodic Protection Inspection and Testing
description: Sources Sought Notice Sources Sought Notice Page 4 of 4 Sources Sought Notice *= Required Field Sources Sought Notice Page 1 of 4 Network Contracting Office 8 (NCO 8) for the Orlando VA Healthcare System is conducting market research to gain knowledge of potential qualified sources to perform Annual Cathodic Protection Inspection & Testing for the Orlando VA Healthcare System (OVAHCS), located at 13800 Veterans Way, Orlando, FL 32827. This is a market research/sources sought synopsis only, (not a pre-solicitation notices pursuant to FAR Part 5). This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is for planning/information purposes only and shall not be construed as a commitment or a promise of a contract by the Government. This is not a solicitation. This notice does not constitute a Request for Bid, Request for Quote or Request for Proposal, nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparation of a response to this notice. The purpose of this notice is for market research purposes only and to make appropriate acquisition decisions to gain knowledge of potential qualified businesses and their Small Business Administration (SBA) size classification in relation to North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 541380 Testing Laboratories and Services with a size standard of $19.0 Million. Project scope: The Contractor shall perform annual inspecting, testing and evaluation of the existing galvanic cathodic protection (CP) system serving the underground coated steel steam and condensate pipelines at the Orlando VA Medical Center, Lake Nona Campus. The purpose of this testing is to verify continued compliance with NACE cathodic protection criteria, ensure electrical isolation integrity, check anode performance, and document all monitoring results in a comprehensive annual report. Large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this survey. This survey is to determine the capability of potential sources and the availability of commercial sources and services pursuant to FAR Part 10. title: Airport BAER Weed Treatment
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 127EAT27Q0004 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Airport BAER Weed Survey and Treatment. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 115310 The small business size standard is $11.5M This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. Statement of Requirement The purpose of this project is to procure services to survey and treat target non-native plants in areas affected by the 2024 Airport Fire. The contractor will survey and treat up to 200 acres of areas impacted by the Airport Fire on the Trabuco Ranger District of the Cleveland National Forest. Survey and treatment areas will include: trails, meadow areas, Forest road sides, riparian areas, chaparral, and campgrounds. Surveys and treatments will prioritize known non-native weed infestations that were impacted by the fire and fire suppression activities. Period of Performance for this requirement is date of award through 30 September 2027. Quotes shall be submitted to megan.acord@usda.gov and are due no later than November 30, 2026 at 12:00 PM MT. Please include the solicitation name and number as the subject line of the email. Questions Questions shall be submitted via email to megan.acord@usda.gov and are due no later than November 23, 2025, at 12:00 PM Pacific Time. This will ensure enough time to respond before the solicitation period ends. Please include the solicitation name and number as the subject line of the email. Quotes shall be submitted via email to megan.acord@usda.gov and are due no later than November 30, 2026, at 12:00PM MT Time. Please include the solicitation name and number as the subject line of the email.

title: HANGAR 140 RENOVATIONS AT NAVAL AIR STATON (NAS) JACKSONVILLE (JAX), JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA
description: The H140 Renovations project scope encompasses the entire 111,000 SF facility, including the Administration, Shops, and Maintenance wings (O1 and O2 spaces) as well as the Organizational Hangar (OH space). The O spaces will include space reconfiguration and replacement of finishes, ceiling systems, lighting and plumbing fixtures. Work also includes replacement of the sliding steel hangar bay doors. Building envelope work will replace the high-bay clerestory windows with high-efficiency thermal windows and provide repair or replacement of walls, cladding, windows, doors. Roofing systems over the hangar high bay, and administration wings will be replaced, while exterior envelope rehabilitation will address hazardous material removal, concrete and masonry repair, and sealing and recoating of surfaces. Replaced building envelope components will be designed to achieve hurricane resistance, Anti-Terrorism Force Protection compliance, and weather-tight performance, but do not entail modifications to the structure. Also included to replace three bridge cranes, two 5 Ton and one 2 Ton. The anticipated performance period for this contract will be 945 calendar days. The magnitude of construction is between $50,000,000 and $100,000,000. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this solicitation is 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, PSC Z2JZ - Repair or Alteration of Miscellaneous Buildings with a Small Business Size Standard of $45 million (M). Under the FAR guidelines, the prime contractor must have the capability to perform at least 15 percent of the contract work with its own employees. The anticipated award date is Fourth Quarter FY 27. Interested sources are invited to respond to this sources sought announcement. Capability Statements consisting of appropriate documentation will be accepted providing it contains ALL the information required below (items 1-6). Complete submission package shall not exceed 4 pages. The information which must be contained in your response is as follows: 1) Contractor Information: Name and address of company, point of contact with phone number and email address. 2) Type of Business: Identify the company�s business size and socio-economic status (HUBZone, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.), if applicable for NAICS Code 236220 applicable to this sources sought. If your firm is claiming HUBZone or 8(a) status, provide a copy of your SBA certification. 3) Bond Capacity: Information must include surety�s name, point of contact, telephone number, email address, and the bonding capacity of at least $50 Million per project, and the maximum aggregate bonding. 4) System for Award Management (SAM): Evidence of registration in the SAM, including Cage Code and Entity Identifier (formerly DUNS Number). 5) Interest: Indicate if a solicitation is issued will your firm/company be submitting a proposal: _____ Yes ______No. 6.) Existing Contract Vehicles your firm may have (GWAC, FSS, MACC, MATOC, etc.) available for this work. 7.) Experience Submission Requirements: Responders shall provide a minimum of two (2) to a maximum of three (3) projects including contract numbers, project titles, dollar amounts, project completion dates, performance ratings, and evidence of specific capabilities listed below: Demonstrate Prime Contractor experience constructing or repairing an industrial facility that was self-performed. Projects submitted for the Offeror shall be valued at approximately $50 million or greater, similar in size, scope and complexity to the proposed hangar repairs and completed and accredited/certified within the past five (5) years of the date of issuance of this announcement. Provide a brief description including completion date and final contract value. If they are not approximately equal to the requested dollar value, identify the dollar value and explain in no more than one paragraph why we should consider the project. The response to this sources sought is not expected to be a proposal, but rather short statements regarding the company�s ability to demonstrate existing-or-developed expertise and experience in relation to the areas specified herein. Submission of Capabilities statement is not a prerequisite to any potential future offerings, but participation will assist the Government in tailoring requirements to be consistent with industry capabilities. After completing its analysis, the Government will determine whether to limit competition among 8(a), HubZone, SDVOSB, VOSB, WOSB, and/or Small Business firms or to proceed with issuing an unrestricted solicitation, inviting full and open competition. Please respond to this announcement no later than 30 November 2026, NLT 2:00 PM Eastern Standard Time via email to Delcheia Turner, Delcheia.l.turner.civ@us.navy.mil and Aimee Johnson, aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil. title: PLA RFI for Hangar 140 Renovations at NAS JAX, Jacksonville, FL.
description: Project Labor Agreement (PLA) Request for Information (RFI) for Construction Project for building in the State of Florida Hangar 140 Renovations at Naval Air Station (NAS) Jacksonville, Jacksonville, FL. This is a request for information/market survey. This is not a request for proposal, request for quote, or an invitation for bid. There will be no solicitation, specification, or drawings available at this time. Naval Facilities Engineering System Command (NAVFAC) SE is soliciting comments from the public addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for the following construction project. The construction project is for the renovation the entire 111,000 SF facility, including the Administration, Shops, and Maintenance wings (O1 and O2 spaces) as well as the Organizational Hangar (OH space). The O spaces will include space reconfiguration and replacement of finishes, ceiling systems, lighting and plumbing fixtures. Work also includes replacement of the sliding steel hangar bay doors. Building envelope work will replace the high-bay clerestory windows with high-efficiency thermal windows and provide repair or replacement of walls, cladding, windows, doors. Roofing systems over the hangar high bay, and administration wings will be replaced, while exterior envelope rehabilitation will address hazardous material removal, concrete and masonry repair, and sealing and recoating of surfaces. Replaced building envelope components will be designed to achieve hurricane resistance, Anti-Terrorism Force Protection compliance, and weather-tight performance, but do not entail modifications to the structure. Also included to replace three bridge cranes, two 5 Ton and one 2 Ton. The project located in the State of Florida. Project will be design-bid-build. NAICS Code: 236220. The magnitude of construction is anticipated to be $50,000,000 - $100,000,000. General period of performance is anticipated to be approximately 945 calendar days. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement as described in 29 U.S.C. 158 (f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) policy states: Executive Order (E.O.) 14063, Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects, requires agencies to use PLAs in large-scale construction projects (defined as a construction projects with a total estimated cost at or above $35M) to promote economy and efficiency in the administration and completion of Federal construction projects. When awarding a contract in connection with a large-scale construction project, agencies shall require use of a PLA for contractors and subcontractors engaged in construction on the project, unless an exception(s) at FAR 22.502-2(d) applies. Reference is made to: FAR Subpart 22.5 Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects; provision, FAR 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement; and to clause, FAR 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. In consideration of the above factors, and any others which may be deemed appropriate, the public is invited to provide responses on the use of a PLA for this construction project utilizing the attached questionnaire. This is not an announcement of the availability of a solicitation nor is it a means of generating a plan holder�s list. This survey is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a Request for Proposal or as an obligation on the part of the Government. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this market survey or otherwise pay for the requested information. The Government will not provide a debriefing on the results of this survey. All information will be held in a confidential manner and will only be used for the purposes intended. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. Responses shall be submitted on the attached questionnaire via email to Delcheia Turner, Delcheia.l.turner.civ@us.navy.mil and Aimee Johnson aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 2:00 pm Eastern Time on November 30, 2026.

title: Multi-Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities on DDG-51 Class Ships Homeported in Norfolk, VA
description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Maritime (PAEM) is issuing solicitation N00024-26-R-4439 to procure a series of Multiple Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities (ISRAs) on DDG-51 Class ships homeported in Norfolk, VA. Fixed Price with Award Fees (FPAF) Contracts will be awarded across Facilitized and Non-Facilitized Lots. Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and CNO scheduled ISRAs, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and ISRAs including, but not limited to, inter-availability preparation and administration (IAPA) support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all delivery orders for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities will be performed at the Government facility and all ISRAs will be performed in-plant at a Contactor-provided facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot on a full and open basis. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Non-Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities only, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are not scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities including, but not limited to, IAPA support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all Delivery Orders will be performed at the Governments facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot as a Small Business Set Aside. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Non-Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Each contract will include three (3) one-year ordering periods. The supply being procured is the repaired, mission-ready vessel, which is returned to service within the Fleet. This solicitation is issued electronically via PIEE and interested offerors should monitor PIEE and SAM.gov for any applicable solicitation amendments, thereafter. This posting does not include all relevant attachments. description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT, A MARKET SURVEY FOR WRITTEN INFORMATION ONLY TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL OFFERORS FOR A DESIGN-BID-BUILD CONSTRUCTION PROJECT TO CONSTRUCT HANGAR 140 RENOVATIONS AT NAVAL AIR STATON (NAS) JACKSONVILLE (JAX), JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR AN INVITATION FOR BID. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation currently available. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. The reference number for this posting is N6945027RH140. The purpose of this notice is for the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) to gain knowledge of ALL qualified and interested parties. All socioeconomic categories are encouraged to respond: U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) certified 8(a), SBA certified HUBZone, woman-owned small business (WOSB), veteran-owned small business (VOSB), and service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB). Potential sources should have current relevant qualifications, experience, personnel, and capability to perform this proposed project. The Government may use the sources sought responses along with other market research to make various determinations regarding the procurement. Project Description: The H140 Renovations project scope encompasses the entire 111,000 SF facility, including the Administration, Shops, and Maintenance wings (O1 and O2 spaces) as well as the Organizational Hangar (OH space). The O spaces will include space reconfiguration and replacement of finishes, ceiling systems, lighting and plumbing fixtures. Work also includes replacement of the sliding steel hangar bay doors. Building envelope work will replace the high-bay clerestory windows with high-efficiency thermal windows and provide repair or replacement of walls, cladding, windows, doors. Roofing systems over the hangar high bay, and administration wings will be replaced, while exterior envelope rehabilitation will address hazardous material removal, concrete and masonry repair, and sealing and recoating of surfaces. Replaced building envelope components will be designed to achieve hurricane resistance, Anti-Terrorism Force Protection compliance, and weather-tight performance, but do not entail modifications to the structure. Also included to replace three bridge cranes, two 5 Ton and one 2 Ton. The anticipated performance period for this contract will be 945 calendar days. The magnitude of construction is between $50,000,000 and $100,000,000. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this solicitation is 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, PSC Z2JZ - Repair or Alteration of Miscellaneous Buildings with a Small Business Size Standard of $45 million (M). Under the FAR guidelines, the prime contractor must have the capability to perform at least 15 percent of the contract work with its own employees. The anticipated award date is Fourth Quarter FY 27. Interested sources are invited to respond to this sources sought announcement. Capability Statements consisting of appropriate documentation will be accepted providing it contains ALL the information required below (items 1-6). Existing Contract Vehicles your firm may have (GWAC, FSS, MACC, MATOC, etc.) available for this work. 7.) Experience Submission Requirements: Responders shall provide a minimum of two (2) to a maximum of three (3) projects including contract numbers, project titles, dollar amounts, project completion dates, performance ratings, and evidence of specific capabilities listed below: Demonstrate Prime Contractor experience constructing or repairing an industrial facility that was self-performed. Projects submitted for the Offeror shall be valued at approximately $50 million or greater, similar in size, scope and complexity to the proposed hangar repairs and completed and accredited/certified within the past five (5) years of the date of issuance of this announcement. Provide a brief description including completion date and final contract value. If they are not approximately equal to the requested dollar value, identify the dollar value and explain in no more than one paragraph why we should consider the project. The response to this sources sought is not expected to be a proposal, but rather short statements regarding the company�s ability to demonstrate existing-or-developed expertise and experience in relation to the areas specified herein. When awarded the TO the Contractor will complete any additional design efforts required by the project and produce a set of working documents for use during construction. Construction only method will include the Government providing 100% design package, including the SOW, drawings, specification, and any other documents as necessary to establish requirements for the work to be accomplished. When awarded the TO the Contractor shall commence with construction in accordance with the design and contract requirements. The Contractor is required to furnish all materials, labor, plant, tools, transportation, equipment, testing services, quality control, and incidentals necessary to provide a complete useable end product as specified in the TO/project documents. title: Y1PZ--Albuquerque National Cemetery Project
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE for Market Research ONLY. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is for market research purposes only in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 and FAR 15.201(e), to determine the availability and technical capabilities of qualified sources. It does not constitute a solicitation and is not to be considered as a commitment by the Government. All firms responding to this notice are advised that their response to this notice is not a request that will be considered for contract award. All interested parties will be required to respond to the resultant solicitation separately from their response to this notice. The purpose of this project is to enable an existing national cemetery to continue to provide burial services for eligible veterans in Central New Mexico. Located in Bernalillo County, about 15 miles west of downtown Albuquerque and serving a population of approximately 235,000 Veterans in the county. This proposed development will provide an additional 15 years of continued burial service to a veteran population who has been served by the Santa Fe National Cemetery. This project will consist of Phase 1 Gravesite Development construction for this cemetery. Phase 1 provides not only for the initial 15-year gravesite burial inventory but also provides for the supporting facilities and infrastructure necessary to maintain and operate the cemetery. The remainder of the site will be developed in future phased projects in accordance with the cemetery master plan. This investment will develop approximately 55 acres of the approximately 585-acre anticipated land acquisition site and provide approximately 28,212 gravesites, including both casket, cremation, natural burial, and memorial wall spaces. This project will provide for the following elements and features: CLIN 0001 Base Bid General Construction: The Base Bid work of this contract includes phased requirements. title: QuidelOrtho Vitros XT 7600 Replenishment / Supplies
description: Pre-Solicitation Notice Notice of Intent to Sole Source Background: The United States Naval Ship (USNS) Comfort (T-AH 20) is a 1,000-bed hospital ship that provides rapid response capability for Combat Casualty Care, Humanitarian Assistance, and Disaster Relief operations worldwide. USNS Comfort provides the National Command Authority with unparalleled healthcare capability in support of America�s strategic interests. To support its clinical laboratory mission, USNS Comfort (T-AH 20), home port Naval Station Norfolk, VA, operates the QuidelOrtho VITROS� XT 7600 Integrated System, a high-throughput, waterless clinical laboratory analyzer that combines digital chemistry imaging and immunodiagnostic testing. Need: The Government requires a one shipment for quantities of supplies necessary to support projected laboratory testing requirements. The Contractor shall furnish 100 percent of the Government-approved quantities shown below for each this purchase, except where shipment of the full quantity is not feasible due to OEM shelf-life, storage, packaging, or transportation limitations. In such cases, the Contractor shall notify the Government and obtain approval prior to making any split shipment. The Contractor shall: Furnish all supplies identified in this SOW and the applicable Bill of Materials. Provide only OEM supplies suitable for their intended use upon delivery. Ensure all delivered items are compatible with the QuidelOrtho VITROS XT 7600 Integrated Systems. Package, handle, transport, and deliver all items in accordance with applicable OEM requirements. Coordinate shipment timing with the designated Government representative prior to shipment. Notify the Government promptly of any actual or anticipated supply constraint, discontinuance, backorder, or shelf-life issue affecting performance. Not provide substitute, additional, or non-scope items without prior written authorization from the Contracting Officer. Out-of-Scope Requirements Products, supplies, or services not specifically identified in this SOW or the applicable Bill of Materials are outside the scope of this requirement. The Contractor shall not furnish substitute, additional, or non-scope items without prior written authorization from the Contracting Officer. A verbal discussion, inquiry, recommendation, or notice shall not constitute authorization. Technical Consumable Classifications & Bill of Materials General The supply requirement shall consist of product categories specific to the VITROS XT 7600 systems. All materials supplied under this requirement shall meet applicable OEM specifications and be fully compatible with the supported analyzers. The detailed Bill of Materials shall identify the required items, part numbers, units of issue, and quantities for this shipment on or before 14 December 2026. Mechanical & Fluid Consumables (Disposable Plastics & System Packs) Item Code / Description Form Factor / Packaging Primary Function / Onboard Specification Vitros VersaTips Mutli-racks packs (Bulk case) Single-use sample aspiration/dispense tips: 2,000 onboard capacities Vitros MircoTips Strip packs / cartridges Specialized pipette tips for liquid chemistry dispensing; onboard capacity: 384 tips Vitros Cuvettes Stack packs Reaction vessels for MicroTip liquid chemistries; onboard capacity: 348 cuvettes Microsample Cups (0.5 mL & 2.0 mL) Bulk cases Pediatric, low-volume, and standard STAT secondary aliquot cups Universal Sample Trays & Inserts Trays accommodating 5/7/10 ML Sample management carriers for routine loading rings and STAT rack position Waste Disposal Bags / Solid Waste Liners Custom-fit biohazard heavy-gauge liner Solid waste collection bins for spent dry slides, used tips, and reaction cuvettes Printer Paper & Optical Cleaner Direct OEM accessories Maintenance and system audit documentation consumables System Operational Fluids & Reagent Packs Item Code / Product Name Nominal Packaging Functional Role & Onboard Storage Requirements VITROS Signal reagents Multi-Pack kit (Reagent A & B) Chemiluminescent substrate for MircoWell assays; onboard capacity: 3 Packs; replenishment on-the-fly. VITROS Universal Wash Reagent 5.0L Container Box Onboard liquid wash buffer for MircoWell immunometric bead washing; onboard capacity: 5.0L Electrolyte Reference Fluid (EFR) Reagent Bottles / Packs Direct potentiometric measurement reference fluid for ISE Mirco Slides; Onboard: 800 Tests Immuno-Wash Fluid (IWF) Pre-Filled Wash Packs Conditioning and wash fluid for MircoWell immune-incubation blocks; onboard: 300 Tests Specialty Diluents & Reconstitution Fluids Vials / Assay-Specific Packs Automated onboard reflex dilutions and off-board sample preparation matrices Diagnostic Assays & Reagents: The contractor shall supply the completed testing menu required by the facility, encompassing: XT MircoSlides & Single MircoSlides: Metabolic & Renal Panels: BUN/Urea, Creatinine, Electrolytes (Na+, K+, Cl-, CO2), Calcium, Phosphorus, Glucose Liver Enzymes & Proteins: ALT, AST, ALP, Total Bilirubin, Direct Bilirubin, Albumin, Total Protein Lipid Profiles: Cholesterol, Triglycerides, HDL, LDL Enzymes & Miscellaneous: CK, Amylase, Lipase, LDH, Uric Acid MircoTip Liquid Reagents: Specific proteins (e.g., CRP, hs-CRP, HbA1c, Ferritin) Therapeutic Drug Monitoring (TDM) and Toxicology: (e.g., Gentamicin, Vancomycin, Methotrexate, Digoxin, Valproic Acid) MicroWell Chemiluminescence Immunoassays: Cardiac Markers: High-sensitivity Troponin I (hs-cTnI), NT-proBNP, CK-MB, Myoglobin Thyroid Panel: TSH, Free T3, Free T4, Total T3, Total T4 Infectious Disease & Serology: Hepatitis markers, HIV combo Reproductive Endocrinology & Oncology: Total B-hCG, PSA, CEA, CA_125, Ferritin, Folate, Vitamin D, Vitamin B12 Calibrators & Quality Control Materials Barcoded Calibrator Kits: Multiplexed and single analyte calibrator kits matching the MircoSlide, MircoTip, and MircoWell Lots Master Lot Data Disks / Barcodes: Machine-readable parameters providing calibration coefficients and curve parameters for up to 25 lots per assay Routine Multi-level Controls: Daily tri-level liquid/lyophilized clinical chemistry, immunoassay, and specialty urine/cardiac control set Bill of Material Control The Bill of Materials shall govern the specific items, part numbers, units of issue, and annual quantities to be delivered under this requirement. Narrative descriptions in this SOW define scope and technical intent only and shall not, by themselves, authorize delivery of items not expressly identified in the contract or applicable Bill of Materials This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. Sources interested in responding to this notice are required to submit a capability statement that includes management and technical data and price information, in sufficient detail and with convincing evidence that clearly demonstrates the capability to perform the required work. Capability statements shall not exceed five (8.5 x 11 inch) pages using a font size no smaller than 10-point. All capability statements received by the due date of this notice will be considered by the Government. A request for documentation or additional information will not be considered as an affirmative response or acceptance of the capability statement. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct competitive procurement or to proceed with a sole source contract. Capability statements should also include the business size and cage code. Capability statements are due by 2:00 PM Local Time, 30 November 2026. Capability statements shall be submitted by e-mail ONLY as a Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF attachment to the following address: curtis.e.cardoza.civ@us.navy.mil.
